[BugFix][Quantization] Fail fast on MXFP checkpoints for devices without an MX matmul (#21893)

Refs #21604

### What this PR does / why we need it?

MXFP-quantized ModelSlim **weight** checkpoints (`W8A8_MXFP8`,
`W4A8_MXFP`,
`W4A4_MXFP4`, `W4A16_MXFP4`) always quantize with the A5 MX kernel, so
they can
only execute on Ascend 950. On A2/A3 the failure used to surface deep
inside
weight loading as an obscure aclnn error (aclnnNpuFormatCast 161002)
after the
whole checkpoint had been read, leaving no hint that the device cannot
run the
checkpoint as published.

This PR rejects such checkpoints at scheme construction: a shared
`require_mx_weight_format(WeightFormat)` helper in `methods/base.py`,
called from
every MXFP weight-scheme `__init__`, raises `NotImplementedError` with
the
quant-format name and actionable remediation (re-quantize with
ModelSlim, e.g.
`W8A8_DYNAMIC`, or deploy on Ascend 950).

This extends the principle of #21604 (native block-wise FP8 checkpoints
are
rejected on non-950 devices) to the sibling ModelSlim path, which
`fp8_block`
never sees. The op-level runtime guards in `device_op.py` ("MXFP MoE
quantization
is only supported on Ascend A5.") stay untouched as the last line of
defense, so
the two layers form defense in depth rather than duplicate checks.

Scope notes, stated up front:

1. The C8-MXFP KV cache (`--kv-cache-dtype mxfp8`) is deliberately
**not** gated
in `kv_cache/mxfp_c8.py`. `AscendC8MXFPKVCacheAttentionMethod` is only
   constructed when that dtype is set (`modelslim_config.py`,
`enable_mxfp_c8_quant`), and the KV-cache path already rejects
unsupported
cache dtypes (`attention_v1.py`, `kv_cache_dtype_str_to_dtype`), so a
gate
inside the method would duplicate an existing check.
`kv_cache/mxfp_c8.py` is
   unchanged in this PR.
2. A checkpoint declaring MXFP quant types is rejected as a whole;
partial
fallback is not attempted, consistent with #21604's approach for native
FP8.

An e2e negative test was not added because the e2e harness requires real
950
hardware for MXFP scheme registration; the scheme-level UT covers the
rejection
path. (For context, the mxfp_compat compatibility shim was removed by
#13447;
the current main tree has no mxfp_compat module or `ensure_mxfp*`
helpers.)

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Loading a ModelSlim MXFP checkpoint on Ascend A2/A3 or Atlas 300I
DUO now
fails at model construction with an actionable message, instead of
failing
minutes later inside weight loading with an opaque aclnnNpuFormatCast
error.

### How was this patch tested?

- `pytest tests/ut/quantization/methods/test_mx_weight_format_gate.py` —
21 new
unit tests: the helper's reject/pass branches for both MXFP8 and MXFP4,
one
reject/pass case per MXFP weight-scheme family (W8A8 linear/MoE, the
DeepSeek
sparse variant, W4A8, W4A4, the FlatQuant variant, W4A16), and a
non-MXFP
scheme proving it stays unguarded. The hardware profile is mocked so
both
  branches run on any machine.
- Existing tests that construct MXFP schemes were updated to pin a
profile with
MXFP8 support, same as #21604 did for `test_fp8_block.py`. A
pristine-main vs
patched regression run over the affected quantization/model tests shows
zero
  new failures.
- Real-device (A3) probe: the real hardware profile resolves MXFP8/MXFP4
support
as False and constructing the `W8A8_MXFP8` linear scheme raises the
actionable
  `NotImplementedError`, while `W8A8_DYNAMIC` constructs unaffected.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: both gate branches
(reject/pass) covered
per scheme family; non-MXFP scheme covered as the unaffected control
group.
- [x] **Regression test**: scheme-construction tests now fail without
the gate
mocks; the gate itself fails closed on hardware without MX support.
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: the reject branch of every
gated scheme is
      asserted, including exception type and message content.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: the mocked-profile pattern
matches the one
      #21604 introduced for `test_fp8_block.py`.

+The gate mirrors the block-wise FP8 rejection: schemes whose quant types always

+machine.

[Feature][KV Pool] Reuse GVA layerwise transfer for DS4.1 shared KV (#21949)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

DeepSeek V4.1 stores shared KV only at selected source layers. Use the
existing GVA layerwise worker, task queues, and lifecycle. There is no
new cross-layer transfer mode or worker.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. DS4.1 can use Memcache GVA layerwise pooling via the existing
`backend: "memcache"` and `use_layerwise: true` settings, including
composite Mooncake V2 push with MultiConnector. No new environment
variable or transfer-mode setting is added.

This path requires Model Runner V2 and eager execution
(`--enforce-eager`). TP/PCP are supported; PP/DCP/KVPP and graph replay
remain outside the supported scope. No additional startup guards are
introduced for those unsupported configurations.

### How was this patch tested?

**Hardware validation completed for the deployed PD pooling cases
(2026-11-16, `a995c1cbb`):** P DP4/TP1/PCP4 and D DP16/TP1/PCP1, vLLM
`4ba787ec9959e566d3b587a796dff07673324da5`, DS4.1 Flash 1017 W4A8. PD
layerwise is enabled on both sides; pool layerwise is enabled on P and
disabled on D. P uses eager execution, APC off and bounded replay on; D
uses FULL_DECODE_ONLY, APC off and bounded replay off. DSpark width is
5. The pool is DRAM-only, 200 GiB per node.

+def hook_scope(root, *, composite=True):
+    attn = SimpleNamespace(kv_transfer_cache_names=("cache",)) if composite else SimpleNamespace()
+    context = SimpleNamespace(attn_metadata=object(), no_compile_layers={"layer": attn})
+    scope = {
+        "get_forward_context": lambda: context,
+        "get_kv_transfer_group": lambda: root,
+        "has_kv_transfer_group": Mock(return_value=True),
+        "is_v1_kv_transfer_group": Mock(return_value=True),
+    }

+        "_kv_layer_transfer_connectors",
+        "wait_for_kv_layer_from_connector",
+        "maybe_save_kv_layer_to_connector",
+    ):
+        load(UTILS, name, scope)
+    return scope, context, attn
+
+
+class TestStandardConnectorHooks(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_nested_pd_multi_connector_selects_bound_shared_children(self):

+class MemoryGVAStore:
+    """Copy real CPU tensor descriptors to simulated GVA objects."""
+
+    requires_exists_before_put = True
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.store = self
+        self.pool = bytearray(1 << 20)
+        self.next_gva = 4096
+        self.objects = {}
+        self.published = set()
+        self.leases = set()
+        self.copies = []
+        self.finish_calls = []
+        self.block_address = None
+        self.block_direction = 1
+        self.blocked = threading.Event()
+        self.resume = threading.Event()
+        self.fail_copy = False
+
+    def ensure_initialized(self):
+        pass
+
+    def set_device(self):
+        pass
+
+    def register_buffer(self, *_args):
+        pass
+
+    def close(self):
+        pass
+
+    def exists(self, keys):
+        return [int(key in self.published) for key in keys]
+
+    def batch_is_exist(self, keys):
+        return self.exists(keys)
+
+    def batch_is_readable(self, keys):
+        return [key in self.published for key in keys]
+
+    def batch_alloc(self, keys, sizes, _ttl=0):
+        result = []
+        for key, size in zip(keys, sizes, strict=True):
+            if key not in self.objects:
+                self.objects[key] = (self.next_gva, size)
+                self.next_gva += size
+            result.append(self.objects[key][0])
+        return result
+
+    def batch_copy(self, gvas, addrs, sizes, direction):
+        if direction == self.block_direction and self.block_address in addrs:
+            self.blocked.set()
+            if not self.resume.wait(timeout=5):
+                raise RuntimeError("test copy was not released")
+        if self.fail_copy:
+            return -1
+        self.copies.append((direction, list(addrs)))
+        for gva, addr, size in zip(gvas, addrs, sizes, strict=True):
+            if direction == 0:
+                self.pool[gva : gva + size] = ctypes.string_at(addr, size)
+            else:
+                ctypes.memmove(addr, bytes(self.pool[gva : gva + size]), size)
+        return 0
+
+    def batch_write_finish(self, keys, results):
+        self.finish_calls.append((list(keys), list(results)))
+        self.published.update(key for key, result in zip(keys, results, strict=True) if result == 0)
+        return [0] * len(keys)
+
+    def batch_get_key_info(self, keys, *, for_load=False):
+        return [
+            SimpleNamespace(gva_list=lambda k=key: [self.objects[k][0]], size=lambda k=key: self.objects[k][1])
+            if key in self.published
+            else None
+            for key in keys
+        ]
+
+    def batch_add_lease(self, keys, _ttl=0):
+        self.leases.update(key for key in keys if key in self.published)
+        return [0 if key in self.published else -1 for key in keys]
+
+    def batch_remove_lease(self, keys):
+        self.leases.difference_update(keys)
+        return 0

+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4]

+def execute(relative, scope, *, owner=None, method=None):
+    nodes = ast.parse((ROOT / (PREFIX + relative)).read_text(encoding="utf-8")).body
+    if owner:
+        nodes = next(n for n in nodes if isinstance(n, ast.ClassDef) and n.name == owner).body
+    if method:
+        nodes = [n for n in nodes if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef) and n.name == method]
+    else:
+        nodes = [n for n in nodes if isinstance(n, (ast.ClassDef, ast.Assign))]
+    future = ast.ImportFrom(module="__future__", names=[ast.alias(name="annotations")], level=0)
+    exec(
+        compile(ast.fix_missing_locations(ast.Module(body=[future, *nodes], type_ignores=[])), relative, "exec"), scope
+    )
+    return scope

[BugFix] Exclude host driver install info from Ascend C cache identity (#20737)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Remove the single `/etc/ascend_install.info` entry from
`_candidate_cann_metadata_files()`.

This file records the host driver installation and can be mounted only
when a container starts. Including it in `compiler_environment_hash` can
invalidate the cache produced while building the same image, even though
the operator compiler environment has not changed.

The patch is limited to **one file and one deleted line**. The other
cache inputs and all three hash algorithms retain their existing
behavior.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Build-cache reuse no longer depends on the runtime-mounted host driver
installation record.

### How was this patch tested?

The reporter has verified this minimal fix.

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/24420b7a341af37a9bc3186e6fc6062512e0aa58

Signed-off-by: AuroraEmiya <92282919+AuroraEmiya@users.noreply.github.com>

[CI] Move four A3-560T weekly cases to the nightly matrix (#22175)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

**Background.** These four A3-560T cases have been running only once a
week in the weekly matrix. Moving them to the nightly matrix raises
their verification frequency to once per day, which shortens the
feedback loop for regressions on the 560T pool.

**Change.**

1. Added the four cases to `nightly_config.yaml` under `a3-560t`:

- `a3-560t.single_node`: structured_output_qwen3 (800i-2),
test_qwen3_grid_exceed_65536 (800i-2),
DeepSeek-V4-Flash-w8a8-sleep-wakeup (800i-16)
- `a3-560t.multi_card`: Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8-PP2-TP2 (800i-4)

2. Removed the corresponding four entries from `weekly_config.yaml` (the
`a3-560t` section only).

Scope notes:
- The duplicated registrations of `structured_output_qwen3` and
`test_qwen3_grid_exceed_65536` under the weekly `a3` section (800t pool)
are intentionally **retained**; only the 560T registrations are moved.
- No test files (pytest/yaml) are touched; this is a registration move
only.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. This only changes CI test matrix registration; end users are not
affected.

### How was this patch tested?

N/A - CI configuration change only. Verified both files still parse as
valid YAML and the moved entries land in the expected sections.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing
- [ ] Boundary / edge-case coverage
- [ ] Regression test
- [ ] Error / failure path coverage
- [ ] Meaningful & reliable tests
- [ ] Performance impact

[BugFix][Test] Declare GDN batch-invariance support and cover Qwen3.5-35B-A3B in the TP4 e2e (#19442)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

The TP4 batch-invariance e2e only covered `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B`: all full
attention, MoE routing at 128 experts with no shared expert.
`Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B` is a hybrid MoE whose 40 layers repeat a 3:1
pattern, so 30 are gated-delta-net linear-attention layers and 10 are
full attention, and every layer runs the Qwen3-Next style MoE block with
256 experts, top-8 and one shared expert. MoE routing was therefore
already covered; the GDN layers, the linear/full interleave and that MoE
block were not, even though
`docs/source/user_guide/feature_guide/batch_invariance.md` already lists
the model as supported on A3.

This PR:

- declares batch-invariance support on the Ascend GDN backend
(`AscendGDNAttentionBackend.supports_batch_invariance()`), without which
the new case cannot even start: vLLM #60271 checks every layer's backend
in `init_attn_backend`, Qwen3.5's GDN layers assign the Ascend backend
directly (`patch_qwen3_5` replaces `get_attn_backend`, so the selector's
own check never sees them), and the engine aborted with `RuntimeError:
VLLM batch_invariant mode is not supported for GDN_ATTN.` The GDN family
is also added to `tests/ut/attention/test_batch_invariance_support.py`,
so dropping the declaration again fails a CPU UT;
- moves the BS=1 vs BS=N comparison into
`_assert_bitwise_batch_invariance()` and folds the shared engine kwargs
into `_model()`, so both models share one body and one configuration: a
new model is a marker block plus a one-line wrapper;
- splits the batch-invariance e2e by model family: the Qwen cases live
in `rlhf/consistency/batch_invariant/test_qwen.py`, the shared BS=1 vs
BS=N comparison and the batch-invariant env in
`tests/e2e/common/rlhf/batch_invariant/common.py` (parallel to
`common/rlhf/weight_transfer`), so a new family is one file instead of
growing a single file;
- adds the Qwen3.5 case on the real 40-layer checkpoint with the same
defaults as the Qwen3 case (`max_num_seqs=144`, `max_model_len=8192`,
TP4, bf16, no prefix caching, `cudagraph_capture_sizes=[1, 32, 64]`,
`graph_mode="full_and_piecewise"`). Its `gpu_memory_utilization` is 0.9,
env-overridable; that is the value it was measured with at TP4. No
layer-reduced slice and no per-case memory cap: with ten full-attention
layers the per-layer fused-attention workspace is the KV cache divided
by ten, so the slice's "cache twice" constraint does not apply;
- keeps the original `pytest.skip` when `RequestOutput` carries no
logprobs, and does not add assertions on the served config;
- fixes the existing case's `e2e_coverage(hardware=...)`: it claimed
`A2`, but `four_card` tests route to `a3-4`, and every other `four_card`
case says `A3`.

No release-note fragment: this is a bugfix, not a user-facing feature.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes, in behaviour: `Qwen3.5-35B-A3B` can start and run with
`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` on Ascend again; before this PR the engine
refused to start because the GDN backend did not declare batch-invariant
support. No API or configuration change.

### How was this patch tested?

CI on the four-card A3 runner, one pytest process for the whole file:

```bash
export VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn VLLM_TEST_TP_SIZE=4
python -m pytest tests/e2e/pull_request/four_card/rlhf/consistency/batch_invariant/test_qwen.py -sv
```

The full-40-layer version of this case already ran green on both vLLM
lanes (`2 passed` per lane, ~6 min each): token ids and the float32
logprobs of the sampled tokens are bitwise equal for 32 prompts between
BS=1 and one BS=32 batch. The current revision only moves the shared
kwargs into `_model()` and drops the per-case assertions, so it is the
same engine configuration; CI on this head is the confirmation.

### Checklist

- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: New tests assert real behavior
and are not written merely to satisfy CI.
- [ ] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: not applicable, the case
mirrors the existing batch-invariance scenario.
- [x] **Regression test**: the GDN backends are added to
`tests/ut/attention/test_batch_invariance_support.py`; the new e2e case
is the end-to-end half.
- [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: not applicable.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: not applicable, e2e test and a class-level
declaration.

[Test] Focus PD combination coverage on the V2 pull Scheduler regression (#19610)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Adds a real-`Scheduler` regression for the V2 Mooncake pull connector
(`MooncakeConnectorV2`) under PD disaggregation with speculative
decoding, as requested in #10654. Part of the external contributor task
pool #9079.

The producer scheduler truncates the last prompt token **before** the
local prefix-cache lookup — for every speculative configuration
(disabled / MTP / DSpark) — so prefix-cache hit counts stay consistent
with the scheduled prompt. The regression drives the real `Scheduler`
(`add_request` → `schedule` → `update_from_output`) with mocked
transport only: the worker handshake thread is stubbed and remote
completion is injected through `KVConnectorOutput`.

Reworked per the review of the initial revision:

- Rebased onto current main; the V2 pull Scheduler regression is now the
single focus of this PR, placed under
`tests/ut/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake/`.
- Kept the boundary cases that exercise the real `Scheduler`: prompt
lengths 512/513/514 around the truncation boundary (warm / hit / shorter
/ longer runs), each ending with `assert_scheduler_empty`.
- The `Scheduler` construction mutates process-global state; the test
now snapshots and restores the KVCacheSpec registry
(`vllm.v1.kv_cache_spec_registry`) and the prefix-cache hash state
(`NONE_HASH` / `_NONE_HASH_SEED`) after the run, so later tests observe
the pristine state.
- Dropped from the first revision: the legacy connector additions, the
KVPP e2e cases, and the reviewer notes tied to them (the e2e directory
layout note and the cross-file `sys.modules` pollution finding — happy
to report the pollution one separately if maintainers prefer). A
topology / rank-mapping follow-up for supported V2 pull/push
configurations will be sent separately.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. Tests only.

### How was this patch tested?

Unit tests, CPU-mock mode (CI-isomorphic): vllm at the current verified
main commit `24420b7a3`, vllm-ascend on this branch rebased onto main
`d476b0097`.

- New file alone: 3 passed (spec-decode disabled / MTP / DSpark).
- `tests/ut/distributed/kv_transfer/` +
`tests/ut/kv_offload/mooncake_v2/`: 950 passed without the new file, 953
passed with it — zero regressions.
- Reverse ordering (`mooncake_v2` + hybrid reference first, the new file
last): 895 passed / 0 failed.
- Global-state restoration verified by a throwaway probe test run after
the regression in the same session (registry dicts and hash seed back to
pristine values, `NONE_HASH` removed).
- Full `tests/ut` sweep on top of main: only pre-existing
local-environment failures, identical with and without this change.
- `pre-commit` (ruff check/format, typos, codespell): all passed.

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage** — the regression is built around
the 512/513/514 truncation boundary.
- [ ] **Regression test** — no bug fixed here; this is a preventive
guard for existing truncation behavior.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests** — exercises the real `Scheduler`;
only the transport is mocked.

[BugFix][Attention] Rebind FIA workspace query in batch invariant mode (#21176)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

`enable_batch_invariant_mode()` swaps
`torch_npu.npu_fused_infer_attention_score` for the
batch-invariant packet, but leaves
`torch_npu._npu_fused_infer_attention_score_get_max_workspace`
pointing at the non-batch-invariant helper. `full_graph_fia()` in
`vllm_ascend/attention/attention_v1.py` sizes the FIA workspace with
that helper and then
registers the task for the batch-invariant kernel, so the two disagree
about the workspace
size.

On Ascend 950 the disagreement is fatal at capture time:

```
call aclnnFusedInferAttentionScoreBatchInvariantV5 failed,
detail: Invalid_Argument(EZ1010):
Value 203456512 for parameter workspaceSize is invalid.
Reason: The passed workspace size 203456512 does not meet the minimum workspace size
487327744 actually required by the AutoContiguous API.
```

194 MiB is allocated for a kernel that needs 465 MiB. It surfaces as
`capture_end ... error code is 107033 ... task group status error`,
which points away from
the real cause: the operator failed inside the graph task group, so
nobody calls
`graph_task_group_end` and `rtStreamEndCapture` reports an unfinished
group. The same model
and configuration with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=0` captures 4/4, which
shows the graph path is
fine and only the two `torch_npu` symbols are out of sync.

This PR binds the workspace query to the batch-invariant counterpart
when the installed
`batch_invariant_ops` exposes it. If the installed package has no such
symbol, it binds a
stub that raises on first use, so full graph capture can never silently
size the workspace
with the non-BI query. Eager and PIECEWISE are unaffected, because they
never call it.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes: batch invariant mode combined with ACL graph capture now works on
A3 and Ascend 950
instead of failing during graph capture. No new API, config key or
environment variable is
added.

### How was this patch tested?

Hardware: Ascend 950DT (8 die), CANN 9.2.1, torch 2.10.0+cpu / torch_npu
2.10.0.post7,
vLLM `ced6857`, vllm-ascend `c09d3e20b`, `batch_invariant_ops` 2.0.0.
Model: Qwen3-30B-A3B (48 layers, 32 Q / 4 KV, head_dim 128, bf16), TP=1,
`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, `HCCL_DETERMINISTIC=strict`,
`enforce_eager=False`
(`cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, capture sizes 1/2/4/8), chunked
prefill and prefix
caching disabled, block size 128.

- before the fix: FULL capture fails on the first bucket with the EZ1010
above; PIECEWISE
  captures 4/4
- after the fix: PIECEWISE 4/4 + FULL 4/4, `fia_graph_calls=192` (48
layers x 4 buckets),
`fia_forward_capturing=192`, no eager FIA call during decode
(`fia_eager_calls=2112` is
  prefill only), `pa_calls=0`, 1240 graph replays
- batch invariance, bitwise (`torch.equal` on token ids, chosen logprob
compared via
`float.hex`, top-5 logprob the same way): repeat 0/2, BS=2/3/4/8 all 0
mismatches, needle
0/24; the same numbers hold in eager mode, and two independent graph
runs are bitwise
  identical
- at runtime the FIA packet is the batch-invariant one and both the
`default` and the `out`
overload report `is_bi=true`; the graph path goes through `out`, so the
captured kernel is
  the BI one

A3 (16 die, `ascend910_9382`), CANN 9.2.0, torch 2.10.0+cpu / torch_npu
2.10.0.post7,
vLLM `24420b7a`, vllm-ascend main, `batch_invariant_ops` built for A3.
Same model, TP=4,
`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, `enforce_eager=False`
(`cudagraph_mode=FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, capture
sizes 1/2/4/8/16), `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`. The gap is wider than
on Ascend 950:

- before the fix: `EZ1010 ... Value 235274240 for parameter
workspaceSize is invalid ...
does not meet the minimum workspace size 820904960`, on all 4 ranks,
capture 0/4
- after the fix: capture 4/4, `full_graph_fia=240` (48 layers x 5
buckets), no EZ1010
- CANN 9.3.0 fails the same way with a slightly different requirement
(820773888) and is
fixed the same way; on CANN 9.1.0 the two queries do not cross the
limit, so capture
  already succeeded there without the change

Scope note on the hardware evidence: the measurement above used an
application-level rebind
of the same two symbols (`import batch_invariant_ops as bops;
torch_npu._npu_fused_infer_attention_score_get_max_workspace =
bops._npu_...`), applied
before engine construction, on both Ascend 950 and A3. This exact commit
has not been
re-run on the device; the code here is those same two assignments moved
into
`enable_batch_invariant_mode()`. Raw logs and
the JSON result files can be attached on request.

Unit tests: two cases in `tests/ut/test_batch_invariant.py` cover the
rebind and the fallback
for builds without the symbol. They were checked locally with `ruff
check` / `ruff format`
v0.14.0 (the version pinned in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`); the NPU unit
test runs in CI.

Note: this makes batch invariant + full graph work for FIA (GQA) models.
MLA / SFA attention
still needs its own batch-invariant kernel coverage, tracked in #5487.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: the change handles the case
where the installed
`batch_invariant_ops` has no workspace query symbol, and a unit test
pins that behavior.
- [x] **Regression test**:
`test_enable_batch_invariant_mode_rebinds_fia_workspace_query`
  fails without the fix (the helper stays on the non-BI function).
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: the fallback path (symbol
missing) is covered.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: the tests assert the rebound
attribute identity, not a
  mock call count.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: not applicable, no hot-path change; the
rebind happens once at
  initialization.

[CI][Misc] Modify cudagraph_mode for step3p7 nightly (#22100)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Setting `cudagraph_mode` to `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` causes a clear prefill
regression for long inputs. For step3p7 the prefill chunk is on the
order of 16k tokens, far above the cudagraph capture limit (288), so
prefill is never replayed from a captured graph in either mode.
`FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` nonetheless splits the compiled prefill graph at
attention boundaries (20+ splitting points) and forcibly disables
`enable_npugraph_ex`, paying per-segment dispatch and synchronization
overhead while gaining none of the benefits of piecewise execution
(which only helps small mixed prefill+decode batches). This PR switches
the default to `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`: prefill is no longer split,
`enable_npugraph_ex` stays enabled, and decode remains covered by the
FULL graph.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
No.
### How was this patch tested?
CI and Nightly tests.

[Refactor][KV Cache] Let MLA and indexer owners publish final MRV2 cache specs (#21370)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

MRV2 currently derives MLA and indexer cache storage formats in the
collector, duplicating information owned by the attention layer and its
backend. This PR moves spec construction to those owners so the
collector receives the final storage format.

- `AscendMLAAttention.get_kv_cache_spec()` preserves upstream metadata,
selects the FA/SFA C8 or TurboQuant format, and reuses the
implementation's packed KV width.
- `AscendSFAIndexerCache` publishes its backend-built spec, including
scale storage and context-parallel replication, while preserving the
disabled-preprocessing and MTP cases.
- The collector applies upstream `customize_attention_spec` to attention
specs, including kernel-block alignment, and retains HiSparse handling.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. This is an internal cache-spec ownership refactor; it adds no
user-facing API, configuration, or operator. No release note fragment is
required.

### How was this patch tested?

Before rebasing, commit `0896b6702` passed **447 targeted unit tests**
in an Ascend A5 container with Python 3.12 and vLLM
`24420b7a341af37a9bc3186e6fc6062512e0aa58`:

```bash
python3 -m pytest -q \
  tests/ut/attention/test_mla_cache_spec.py \
  tests/ut/attention/test_indexer.py \
  tests/ut/worker/test_attn_utils_v2.py \
  tests/ut/core/test_kv_cache_interface.py \
  tests/ut/worker/test_model_runner_v2_mamba.py
```

Coverage includes FA/SFA cache formats, implementation-provided packed
widths, metadata preservation, backend customization and alignment,
indexer preprocessing/MTP cases, context-parallel replication, and
hybrid cache layouts.

Rebased onto main `fb02de0881`, which pins vLLM
`ba15685ab7f4f5fbed8630bbb7441f8837e76fbe`. All 11 commits have
unchanged patches according to `git range-diff`. Ruff 0.14.0 lint and
formatting checks passed for all 15 changed Python files; `git diff
--check` passed.

CI on `3ab32f5ce` passed pre-commit and both CPU unit-test jobs (pinned
main and v0.33). The A2 FLA lazy-import regression failed because
importing the Kimi RecoverSSM record type eagerly loads the Kimi package
and FLA; `853fdb70e` defers that import until model construction. The
existing `tests/e2e/pull_request/one_card/test_fla_lazy_imports.py`
covers this failure. Ruff lint/format and `git diff --check` passed for
the fix. Full `format.sh ci` could not run locally because pre-commit is
unavailable; remote NPU validation is pending because the validation
endpoint is unreachable.

The upstream LoRA job also failed during fixture setup: the runner lacks
the Hugging Face cached snapshot for `vllm-project/self_cognition_Alice`
while `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`. This requires CI cache provisioning. CI
validation of `853fdb70e` is pending. The 447-test result above predates
the dependency upgrade; it is not validation of the new baseline.
End-to-end inference, accuracy, and performance validation have not been
rerun on the current commit.

[Test] Add five-round Kimi-K3 Experts256 A5 nightly coverage (#21284)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Add five-round Kimi-K3 W4A8 E256 accuracy coverage to the A5 nightly
matrix to track accuracy variation across repeated runs.

- Register a single-node, eight-NPU A5 case using the 256-expert
checkpoint.
- Evaluate the first 100 GSM8K questions with the four-shot CoT
configuration, batch size 60, and a maximum output length of 1024
tokens.
- Run five separate pytest instances over the same 100-question subset,
producing 500 evaluations in total.
- Add optional `test_rounds` support to the single-node test harness.
Cases without this setting continue to run once.
- Archive each round's AISBench outputs, benchmark results, logs, and
status under `outputs/nightly_rounds/<case>/round-XX`. Retain the final
round's benchmark results and log archives at the existing
summary/upload locations.
- Add unit tests for round-count validation, configuration isolation,
failure continuation, and artifact preservation.

With normal pytest execution, an ordinary failure in one round does not
prevent later rounds from running; the overall pytest result still
reports the failure.

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

This changes test and CI behavior only.

The new case uses TP8 with expert parallelism, the V2 model runner,
eager BF16 execution, chunked prefill, and FlashComm1. Prefix caching is
disabled. Generation uses temperature 0, top_p 1.0, seed 42, and
thinking_effort low.

The accuracy configuration retains `baseline: 50.0` and `threshold:
50.0`. This accepts scores across the 0–100% range, so the case collects
repeated accuracy measurements rather than enforcing a strict accuracy
regression threshold.

### How was this patch tested?

- Completed pre-commit and CPU unit-test jobs have passed for the
current PR head.
- Added CPU-only regression coverage for invalid round counts,
independent round configurations, and artifact isolation.
- The failure-continuation test intentionally fails round 2 and verifies
that rounds 3–5 still execute, all five statuses are preserved, and the
final summary contains round 5's results.

Hardware accuracy results should be assessed from the corresponding A5
nightly run and its per-round artifacts.

+"""Collect independent pytest rounds and retain their benchmark artifacts."""
+
+import json
+import shutil
+from collections.abc import Iterator, Sequence
+from contextlib import contextmanager
+from copy import deepcopy
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+
+
+def expand_test_rounds(configs: Sequence[Any]) -> list[tuple[Any, int, int]]:
+    rounds = []
+    for config in configs:
+        count = config.extra_config.get("test_rounds", 1)
+        if isinstance(count, bool) or not isinstance(count, int) or count < 1:
+            raise ValueError("test_rounds must be a positive integer")
+        for number in range(1, count + 1):
+            rounds.append((deepcopy(config) if count > 1 else config, number, count))
+    return rounds
+
+
+def round_id(parameters: tuple[Any, int, int]) -> str:
+    config, number, count = parameters
+    return config.name if count == 1 else f"{config.name}-round-{number:02d}-of-{count:02d}"
+
+
+@contextmanager
+def preserve_round(config: Any, number: int, count: int, work_dir: Path) -> Iterator[None]:
+    if count == 1:
+        yield
+        return
+
+    output_root = work_dir / "outputs"
+    # One YAML file may contain several independently repeated cases.
+    case_dir = output_root / "nightly_rounds" / config.name
+    target = case_dir / f"round-{number:02d}"
+    target.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    status = {"name": config.name, "round": number, "total_rounds": count, "outcome": "passed"}
+    print(f"\nNightly round {number}/{count}: {config.name}", flush=True)
+    try:
+        yield
+    except BaseException as error:
+        status.update(outcome="failed", error=f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}")
+        raise
+    finally:
+        # Keep the normal outputs/ upload location while removing AISBench's
+        # previous work directory before the next independent server/test run.
+        for source in output_root.iterdir():
+            if source.name != "nightly_rounds":
+                shutil.move(str(source), str(target / source.name))
+        for name in ("benchmark_results", "log_archives"):
+            source = work_dir / name
+            if source.exists():
+                shutil.move(str(source), str(target / name))
+                if number == count:
+                    # Existing workflow summary/upload steps still see the
+                    # last round; the full history lives in outputs/.
+                    shutil.copytree(target / name, source)
+        for name in ("output_accuracy.txt", "output_performance.txt"):
+            source = work_dir / name
+            if source.exists():
+                shutil.move(str(source), str(target / name))
+        (target / "status.json").write_text(json.dumps(status, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
+        print(f"Nightly round {number}/{count}: {status['outcome']}; artifacts: {target}", flush=True)

[CI][BugFix] Apply existing labels in issue templates (#21954)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Two issue forms under `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE` reference labels that do
not
exist in this repository. GitHub only applies a template label when a
label
with exactly that name exists, so issues opened through these forms
never got
their type label:

| Template | Label before | Label after |
|---|---|---|
| `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/800-others.yml` | `misc` | `question` |
| `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/110-user-story.yml` | `user-story` |
`documentation` |

`question` and `documentation` are the existing type labels that match
the
intent of the two forms: `question` ("a general question; no code change
may be
required") for the catch-all "Others" discussion form, and
`documentation` for
the user story form, whose submission is published on the documentation
site
(`community/user_stories/index.html`).

The usage form keeps `labels: ["usage"]`: the repository label was
renamed to
the lowercase `usage`, so that form matches it again and needs no
change.

The type-label table in
`docs/source/community/issue-workflow-guidelines.md`
lists the same labels and is already consistent with the repository
label
list, so no documentation change is needed.

Fixes #21897

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. Only the repository issue forms change. There is no runtime, API, or
default behavior change, so no release note fragment is required.

### How was this patch tested?

- Queried the repository label list through the GitHub API: the
repository has
no `misc` or `user-story` label, and it does have `question`,
`documentation`
  and `usage`.
- Checked all ten issue templates that declare a `labels` list. The
labels
they now reference are `usage`, `question`, `documentation`,
`installation`,
`bug`, `feature request`, `new model`, `performance` and `RFC`, all of
which
exist in the repository. The remaining three templates declare no label.
- The change is limited to the `labels` list of two YAML forms, so the
forms
  stay valid.

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: all issue templates were
checked
  against the repository label list, not only the two that changed.
- [x] **Regression test**: not applicable; there is no runtime code
path. The
  label list is asserted in the PR description.
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: not applicable; no runtime
behavior
  changed.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: the verification queries the live
repository label list, which is exactly the condition that made the
labels
  fail to apply.
- [x] **Performance impact**: not applicable; configuration only.

[Performance] Pin shared KV mmap and parallelize startup population (#21101)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Native KV tiering uses pageable shared memory and repeats full-region
pre-faulting on replicated MLA workers. Support opt-in pinning of the
existing mapping for direct batched transfers, and distribute worker
pre-faulting across the shared region.

- When pinning is enabled, register each worker's slots for
non-replicated layouts; replicated MLA workers register the complete
shared mapping.
- Reuse upstream's segment count and
`populate_shard=(logical_worker_rank, world_size)` where available.
MLA's data-slot rank remains zero.
- Construct scheduler and worker mappings with identical segment
parameters. Reuse upstream primary/secondary/tiering managers; override
their construction because upstream `get_manager` hardcodes a
single-file region.
- Run `_all_workers_barrier` after worker population, before host
pinning. EngineCore initializes workers before the scheduler: passing
this barrier into the CPU region constructor would unlink files before
the scheduler could attach. Keep backing paths during successful
startup; detach creator-owned names when initialization aborts or during
shutdown.
- Roll back failed registrations, synchronize before unregistering, and
preserve registered views if release fails. Population failure releases
peers; barrier and scheduler-construction failures clean up constructed
resources.

- Keep each shared mapping and its registered tensor views in a
process-scoped registration owner until unregister succeeds. If
construction/rollback fails and the unfinished worker is
garbage-collected, the mapping remains owned until recovery or process
exit. A lock protects registry membership only; synchronization and ACL
calls run outside it.

- Detach creator-owned backing names independently of unmapping when
initialization aborts or shutdown starts. Even failed handler
cleanup/synchronization/unregister cannot skip this unlink step.
Registered mappings remain owned and usable; non-creators leave the
creator files intact. Handle every backing segment and older single-file
mappings.

Uses the existing C++ bindings. No environment variable or
registration-scope configuration was added. Based on upstream main
`9005a22a862a95d52025b70fb2bff8eed8a5a5e3`.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. `TieringOffloadingSpec` supports opt-in shared-mmap pinning on
supported builds and uses parallel population on supported vLLM
versions.

- `pin_shared_mmap` defaults to `false`; set it to `true` to enable host
registration.
- Registration scope follows the cache layout automatically.
- Handle both the older `_REGION_SEGMENTS` and newer `REGION_SEGMENTS`
upstream names.
- `CPUOffloadingSpec` retains its pinned tensor allocator.

Release note: `release_notes/fragments/21101.yaml`.

Usage: [CPU offload
guide](https://github.com/ckeyever/vllm-ascend/blob/79749e52b7bb2e0d198ae5dbd007206ca91203af/docs/source/user_guide/feature_guide/kv_cache_cpu_offload.md#pinning-the-shared-cpu-tier)
documents `pin_shared_mmap` placement, its default, an enable example,
automatic registration scope, fallback behavior and population-time
scaling.

### How was this patch tested?

#### Pinning performance comparison

User-reported pinning enabled/disabled measurements; not independently
rerun on the final PR. These results concern pinning and do not measure
sharded-population startup time.

| Model | Mean TTFT without pin (ms) | Mean TTFT with pin (ms) | Mean
TTFT reduction | Per-byte DMA without pin (GB/s) | Per-byte DMA with pin
(GB/s) | Per-byte DMA improvement |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3-1.7B | 41,284 | 30,114 | 27.06% | 8.23 | 13.27 | +61.24% |
| GLM-5.2 | 209,937 | 195,638 | 6.81% | 1.94 | 2.49 | +28.35% |

Both percentages use the non-pinned result as the baseline:

- Mean TTFT reduction = (TTFT without pin - TTFT with pin) / TTFT
without pin x 100%.
- Per-byte DMA improvement = (DMA with pin - DMA without pin) / DMA
without pin x 100%.

Local CPU validation:

- Opt-in-default follow-up: worker lifecycle coverage includes omitted,
explicitly disabled and explicitly enabled pinning; existing failure
regressions explicitly enable registration. Synchronization/unregister
failure intentionally skips mmap cleanup so the registration owner keeps
the mapping alive.

- After rebasing, 105 tests passed against the current vLLM CI-main
source `ba15685ab7f4f5fbed8630bbb7441f8837e76fbe`.
- After rebasing, 105 tests passed against official vLLM v0.33.0 source
4ba787ec9959e566d3b587a796dff07673324da5, the release selected by
upstream CI.
- Earlier backward-compatibility validation: 101 tests passed against
official vLLM v0.32.0 source; four partial-slot cases are skipped
because it only supports whole-region registration.
- Earlier validation: 86 tests passed against local vLLM source
`a04520a6d4`, exercising its newer public segment constant and
memfd-backed reservation.
- Rebased the linear PR branch onto upstream main
9005a22a862a95d52025b70fb2bff8eed8a5a5e3. Retained main's
DevicePointers/version-compatibility changes together with the PR's
registration-owner lock. The CI preparation command (git rebase onto
this main snapshot) completes without conflicts and leaves HEAD
unchanged. Logical worker-rank slot selection remains independent of
physical device IDs.
- Files under `tests/ut/kv_offload/`: `test_shared_mmap_pinning.py`,
`test_tiering_population.py`, `test_npu_offload_spec.py`, and
`test_native_cpu_offload.py`.
- Four concurrent CPU threads map the actual shared memory, execute real
pre-faults and segment mappings, and use the actual upstream
primary/tiering managers. Tests cover disjoint MLA worker ranges,
ordinary worker slots, a scheduler attaching both before and after
workers, shared-byte visibility, manager caching, and removal of backing
files during teardown.

 - `cpu_bytes_to_use`: Total bytes reserved for the CPU tier across all workers. This is required by the vLLM offloading specs.
 - `blocks_per_chunk`: Number of NPU KV-cache blocks in one offloaded chunk. It must be greater than zero. Alternatively, `block_size` can specify the chunk size in tokens when all KV-cache groups use the same block size; the two options are mutually exclusive.
 - `spec_name`: Use the upstream names `"CPUOffloadingSpec"` for CPU-only offload or `"TieringOffloadingSpec"` for multi-tier offload. vLLM Ascend transparently maps them to the NPU implementations.
+- `pin_shared_mmap`: Boolean, defaults to `false`. Applies to `TieringOffloadingSpec`; set to `true` to register its shared CPU mapping as pinned host memory.
 - `secondary_tiers`: Optional list of vLLM tiering backends used by `TieringOffloadingSpec`. Each entry is a dict; common keys:
     - `type`: Backend type. Use `"fs"` for filesystem storage.
     - `root_dir`: Directory the tier writes block files into.
     - `n_read_threads` / `n_write_threads`: Thread-pool sizes for the tier's I/O. For high-bandwidth backends (e.g. 3FS over RDMA) increasing these helps saturate parallel bandwidth.
 
+### Pinning the shared CPU tier
+
+`pin_shared_mmap` defaults to `false` for `TieringOffloadingSpec`. To enable
+registration on supported Ascend runtimes, set `pin_shared_mmap` to `true` in
+`kv_connector_extra_config`. This registers the existing shared CPU mapping as
+page-locked host memory for direct batched NPU transfers:
+
+```json
+{
+    "kv_connector": "OffloadingConnector",
+    "kv_role": "kv_both",
+    "kv_connector_extra_config": {
+        "spec_name": "TieringOffloadingSpec",
+        "cpu_bytes_to_use": 8589934592,
+        "blocks_per_chunk": 8,
+        "pin_shared_mmap": true,
+        "secondary_tiers": [
+            {"type": "fs", "root_dir": "/tmp/vllm_kv_offload"}
+        ]
+    }
+}
+```
+
+Registration scope follows the cache layout automatically: replicated MLA
+workers register the whole shared region; other layouts register each worker's
+page-aligned slots when the upstream vLLM range API is available, otherwise the
+whole region is registered.
+
+If the Ascend extension lacks the required host-registration/batched-copy APIs,
+or registration fails, the worker rolls back completed registrations and falls
+back to pageable mmap with a warning. Startup logs report the registered bytes
+and range count when registration succeeds.
+
+Larger shared CPU regions require more pages to be populated (pre-faulted),
+so increasing `cpu_bytes_to_use` increases startup population time. On
+supported vLLM versions, segmented mappings and disjoint MLA population shards
+reduce this cost. Population is required even when `pin_shared_mmap` is
+`false`; benchmark startup time separately from KV-transfer bandwidth.
+
+`CPUOffloadingSpec` uses PyTorch's pinned tensor allocator and does not use this
+option.
+

[Refactor]Adopt vLLM pluggable kv-cache-dtype mechanism for KV cache (#21925)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR adopts the pluggable KV cache dtype mechanism introduced in vLLM
(>= releases/v0.33.0). It registers Ascend-specific KV-cache dtype
handlers via `register_kv_cache_dtype`. This allows the Ascend backend
to self-manage kernel dispatch for quantized KV caches (e.g., FP8 and
INT8) natively without relying on legacy platform/worker patches, which
have been removed.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

no

### How was this patch tested?

Tested with existing unit tests and integration tests on Ascend NPU.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [ ] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: I reviewed whether this change
involves
boundary conditions (e.g. empty input, single/zero element, min/max
values,
off-by-one, sequence-length limits, integer overflow). Where applicable,
I
added unit tests covering these edge cases in `tests/ut/` or
`tests/e2e/`.
- [ ] **Regression test**: If this PR fixes a bug, I added a regression
test
  that would fail without the fix.
- [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: I covered abnormal paths
(exceptions,
timeouts, out-of-range, division by zero) in addition to the happy path.
- [ ] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: New tests assert real behavior
and are
  not written merely to satisfy CI.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: If this PR touches a performance-sensitive
path,
  I attached benchmark results and added performance regression tests.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Ascend KV-cache dtype handlers registered via vLLM's
+``register_kv_cache_dtype`` mechanism (vLLM >= releases/v0.33.0).
+
+Importing this module eagerly decorates the handlers, which appends each name
+to ``KV_CACHE_DTYPES``, injects the torch dtype into
+``STR_DTYPE_TO_TORCH_DTYPE`` in place, and stores the handler for later
+``quant_mode()`` / ``is_quantized()`` queries. The in-place dict mutation means
+that once this module is imported (which happens in every process that builds a
+VllmConfig, via the platform's quant-config registration), the upstream
+``kv_cache_dtype_str_to_dtype`` lookup resolves ``"fp8"`` to
+``torch.float8_e4m3fn`` rather than the upstream ``torch.uint8``.
+"""
+
+import torch
+from vllm.config.cache import register_kv_cache_dtype
+from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import KVQuantMode
+
+
+@register_kv_cache_dtype("fp8")
+class Fp8AscendHandler:
+    """fp8 KV cache stored as ``torch.float8_e4m3fn`` on Ascend.
+
+    The upstream builtin ``"fp8"`` maps to ``torch.uint8`` (raw fp8 bytes
+    consumed by NVIDIA cutlass kernels). Ascend's MLA/DSA kernels operate
+    on native ``torch.float8_e4m3fn`` directly, so re-registering ``"fp8"``
+    here flips that mapping to ``float8_e4m3fn``. The decorator logs an
+    ``already exists and will be overwritten`` warning; this is expected
+    and intentional on the Ascend platform.
+
+    No per-token scale: ``quant_mode`` returns ``KVQuantMode.CUSTOM`` so
+    the Ascend backend fully self-manages kernel dispatch rather than
+    reusing an upstream generic fp8/per-token-head kernel path.
+    """
+
+    name = "fp8"
+
+    def torch_dtype(self) -> torch.dtype:
+        return torch.float8_e4m3fn
+
+    def quant_mode(self):
+        return KVQuantMode.CUSTOM
+
+
+@register_kv_cache_dtype("int8")
+class Int8AscendHandler:
+    """int8 KV cache stored as ``torch.int8`` on Ascend."""
+
+    name = "int8"
+
+    def torch_dtype(self) -> torch.dtype:
+        return torch.int8
+
+    def quant_mode(self):
+        return KVQuantMode.CUSTOM
+
+
+@register_kv_cache_dtype("mxfp8")
+class Mxfp8AscendHandler:

[Bugfix] Correct DeepSeek V4.1 DSpark auxiliary layer capture (#22122)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fix auxiliary hidden-state capture for DeepSeek V4.1 DSpark. The MRV2
resolver preserves zero-based checkpoint layer IDs, but the target
previously applied a one-based comparison. For example, IDs [37, 38, 39]
selected the inputs to layers [36, 37, 38].

Capture the selected layer inputs consistently in regular forward and
decoder replay, including when a selected ID equals
decoder_replay_start. This correction also affects fixed DSpark and is
separated from the adaptive-verification changes in #21137.

### How was this patch tested?

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [ ] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: I reviewed whether this change
involves
boundary conditions (e.g. empty input, single/zero element, min/max
values,
off-by-one, sequence-length limits, integer overflow). Where applicable,
I
added unit tests covering these edge cases in `tests/ut/` or
`tests/e2e/`.
- [ ] **Regression test**: If this PR fixes a bug, I added a regression
test
  that would fail without the fix.
- [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: I covered abnormal paths
(exceptions,
timeouts, out-of-range, division by zero) in addition to the happy path.
- [ ] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: New tests assert real behavior
and are
  not written merely to satisfy CI.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: If this PR touches a performance-sensitive
path,
  I attached benchmark results and added performance regression tests.

[Feature] Support prefill KVPP in Mooncake Push (#21805)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Enable prefill-side KVPP with `MooncakePushConnector` for supported
non-hybrid MLA/SFA models, including GLM-5.3 W8A8C8. Push previously
chose a producer replica by destination rank. With KVPP, that rank can
lack the layer's persistent cache, leaving a decode worker with missing
data even after all producer ranks report DONE.

Reuse the owner map from cache registration. A target layer's persistent
owner writes that layer to each decode worker that has it. Replicated
MTP caches still select one producer per destination. Decode keeps KVPP
disabled.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Set `"enable_kvpp": true` on the prefill node when both nodes use
`MooncakePushConnector`. Decode leaves KVPP disabled. Prefill uses DCP=1
when KVPP is enabled. Decode can use the existing Push DCP path with
compatible cache layouts.

### How was this patch tested?

- **Local CPU/mock** — Used the workspace's existing
`vllm-ascend/.venv`, the base branch's pinned vLLM source
(`24420b7a341af37a9bc3186e6fc6062512e0aa58`), and a temporary dependency
overlay for Transformers 5.20.2, huggingface-hub 1.33.0 and tokenizers
0.23.3. The default environment failed collection due to a Transformers
mismatch. With the overlay, `uv run --active pytest -q
tests/ut/kv_offload/mooncake_v2 tests/ut/test_ascend_config.py -k
'mooncake_v2 or KVPP'` reported **681 passed, 159 deselected, 27
subtests passed**.
- **A3 host (.5), Mooncake V2 unit suite** — `python3 -m pytest -q
--noconftest tests/ut/kv_offload/mooncake_v2` reported **675 passed** on
the clean PR tree. The new regression uses P TP2 × PCP2 and D TP2. It
checks bytes and exactly one write per destination cache component for
every required target layer, LI C8 keys and scales, and the selected MTP

values. Full-model serving was outside this smoke test.

eager mode. Ran Prefill with TP2 and Decode with TP1 on three NPUs on

greedy requests of 5, 563, and 527 input tokens, each generating 24

KVPP enabled, the two Prefill ranks advertised 14 and 13 persistent
cache layers, and Decode registered all 27 layers.

passed.

[Refactor][SpecDecode] Extract shared draft QuaRot helpers into quarot_utils.py (#21783)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Implements [RFC
#21571](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/21571) as a
mechanical extraction (no behavior change).

Qwen3 DFlash2 and the Qwen3, GLM-5, and Kimi K3 DSpark drafts share the
same QuaRot weight-alignment code. Today that code lives in
`qwen3_dspark.py`, so DFlash2 must import a DSpark model module to reach
a weight-loading helper, and cross-draft weight names (e.g. the GLM
checkpoint alias from #21439) have to live inside one model's file.

This PR creates `vllm_ascend/models/quarot_utils.py` and moves the four
shared definitions into it:

- `TARGET_EMBED_WEIGHT_NAMES` / `TARGET_LM_HEAD_WEIGHT_NAMES` (candidate
key order preserved, including the
`model.language_model.embed_tokens.weight` alias from #21439)
- `process_weight()` (projection rotation, verbatim)
- `align_draft_weights()` (embedding / LM-head ownership rules and the
unrotated PP embedding fallback, verbatim; the fallback's migration to
target-side loading stays tracked by RFC #21537)

The Qwen3 DFlash2 and Qwen3 / GLM-5 / Kimi K3 DSpark drafts now import
`align_draft_weights()` from the shared module.
`load_quarot_target_layer()` continues to own checkpoint lookup, TP
vocab slicing, and rotation, unchanged. The new module imports no
DSpark/DFlash model class, so it is importable independently of
`qwen3_dspark.py`.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. Internal refactor only; no release note fragment needed.

### How was this patch tested?

- The moved definitions were verified byte-identical against
`qwen3_dspark.py` at the base revision (`git diff` of the extracted
block is empty).
- The six affected weight-loading test files re-point their monkeypatch
targets to `quarot_utils`; an AST check confirms every patched name
exists in the new module.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format` (v0.14.0, matching
`.pre-commit-config.yaml`) pass on all touched files.
- Two independent reviews (GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash perspectives)
verified import independence (no cycle via `llama_eagle3` /
`vllm_ascend.utils`), no missed consumers (GLM5Next MTP, DeepSeek
V4/V4.1 DSpark, `patch_dspark.py`), and correct mock coverage of both
module namespaces.
- Unit tests were not executed locally (no vllm environment on this
machine); relying on CI cpu-ut as the final gate.

### E2E pre/post validation (requested in review)

Compared **pre-refactor base** `4b3bd7ebe` (upstream/main at the time)
against **PR head** `9c0c68823`.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+"""Shared QuaRot weight-alignment helpers for draft models.
+
+This module must stay importable independently of any DSpark/DFlash
+model module; do not import model classes here.
+"""
+
+import json
+import logging
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import torch
+from safetensors import safe_open
+from torch import nn
+from vllm.distributed import get_pp_group
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.vocab_parallel_embedding import ParallelLMHead, VocabParallelEmbedding
+
+from vllm_ascend.utils import (
+    get_rotation_matrix,
+    get_rotation_path,
+)
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+TARGET_EMBED_WEIGHT_NAMES = (
+    "language_model.model.embed_tokens.weight",
+    "model.language_model.embed_tokens.weight",
+    "model.embed_tokens.weight",
+)
+TARGET_LM_HEAD_WEIGHT_NAMES = (
+    "language_model.lm_head.weight",
+    "lm_head.weight",
+)
+
+
+def _find_safetensors_weight(
+    model_path: Path,
+    weight_names: tuple[str, ...],
+) -> tuple[Path, str]:
+    """Locate one target tensor without loading unrelated checkpoint shards."""
+    for index_path in sorted(model_path.glob("*.safetensors.index.json")):
+        with index_path.open(encoding="utf-8") as index_file:
+            weight_map = json.load(index_file).get("weight_map", {})
+        for weight_name in weight_names:
+            if shard_name := weight_map.get(weight_name):
+                return model_path / shard_name, weight_name
+
+    for shard_path in sorted(model_path.glob("*.safetensors")):
+        with safe_open(shard_path, framework="pt", device="cpu") as shard:
+            shard_keys = set(shard.keys())
+        for weight_name in weight_names:
+            if weight_name in shard_keys:
+                return shard_path, weight_name
+
+    raise KeyError(f"None of {weight_names!r} was found in the target checkpoint at {model_path}.")
+
+
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def load_quarot_target_layer(
+    layer: nn.Module,
+    target_model_path: Path | str,
+    weight_names: tuple[str, ...],
+    rotation: torch.Tensor | None,
+    label: str,
+) -> None:
+    """Load one target vocab shard into the draft's unrotated hidden basis.
+
+    ``rotation=None`` loads the shard unchanged (no QuaRot alignment)."""
+    target_model_path = Path(target_model_path)
+    shard_path, weight_name = _find_safetensors_weight(
+        target_model_path,
+        weight_names,
+    )
+    shard_indices = getattr(layer, "shard_indices", None)
+    if shard_indices is None:
+        start_index = 0
+        end_index = layer.weight.shape[0]
+    else:
+        start_index = shard_indices.org_vocab_start_index
+        end_index = shard_indices.org_vocab_end_index
+
+    with safe_open(shard_path, framework="pt", device="cpu") as shard:
+        target_weight = shard.get_slice(weight_name)[start_index:end_index]
+
+    if rotation is not None:
+        rotation = rotation.to(
+            device=layer.weight.device,
+            dtype=torch.float32,
+        )
+        target_weight = target_weight.to(
+            device=layer.weight.device,
+            dtype=torch.float32,
+        )
+        aligned_weight = torch.matmul(target_weight, rotation.T)
+    else:
+        # No rotation: plain shard copy for drafts that cannot alias the
+        # target layer (e.g. the target embedding on a later PP stage).
+        aligned_weight = target_weight.to(
+            device=layer.weight.device,
+            dtype=layer.weight.dtype,
+        )
+    loaded_rows = aligned_weight.shape[0]
+    layer.weight.data[:loaded_rows].copy_(aligned_weight.to(layer.weight.dtype))
+    layer.weight.data[loaded_rows:].zero_()
+    logger.info(
+        "[spec_decode/quarot] Loaded and aligned %s from %s (%s).",
+        label,
+        shard_path.name,
+        tuple(layer.weight.shape),
+    )
+
+
+# Process the first linear weight with rotation matrix, if the target model uses rotary quantization
+def process_weight(linear_weight: torch.Tensor, rotation_weight: torch.Tensor):
+    assert linear_weight.shape[1] % rotation_weight.shape[0] == 0, (
+        f"Linear weight shape[1] must be a multiple of rotation weight shape[0],"
+        f" but get {linear_weight.shape[1]=} and {rotation_weight.shape[0]=}"
+    )
+    rotation_weight = rotation_weight.to(device=linear_weight.device, dtype=torch.float32)
+    hidden_size = rotation_weight.shape[0]
+    ori_dtype = linear_weight.dtype
+    processed_weight = torch.empty(linear_weight.shape, dtype=torch.float32, device=linear_weight.device)
+    for start_pos in range(0, linear_weight.shape[1], hidden_size):
+        linear_weight_chunked = linear_weight[:, start_pos : start_pos + hidden_size].to(torch.float32)
+        processed_weight[:, start_pos : start_pos + hidden_size].copy_(
+            torch.matmul(linear_weight_chunked, rotation_weight)
+        )
+    return processed_weight.to(ori_dtype)
+
+
+@torch.no_grad()
+def align_draft_weights(model, projection, vllm_config):
+    """Align draft inputs with the rotated target without modifying shared weights."""
+    rotation_path = get_rotation_path(vllm_config)
+    if rotation_path is not None:
+        rotation = get_rotation_matrix(rotation_path).cpu()
+        weight = projection.weight
+        weight.copy_(process_weight(weight.cpu(), rotation).to(weight.device))
+    else:
+        if get_pp_group().world_size == 1:
+            return
+        # PP stages past the first cannot alias the target's stage-0
+        # embedding; load this rank's vocab shard from the target
+        # checkpoint unrotated so the draft owns its copy.
+        rotation = None
+        weight = projection.weight
+    target_config = vllm_config.model_config.hf_text_config
+    for owner, name, layer_cls, weight_names, own_flag in (
+        (model.model, "embed_tokens", VocabParallelEmbedding, TARGET_EMBED_WEIGHT_NAMES, "has_own_embed_tokens"),
+        (model, "lm_head", ParallelLMHead, TARGET_LM_HEAD_WEIGHT_NAMES, "has_own_lm_head"),
+    ):
+        if getattr(model, own_flag, False):
+            continue
+        if rotation is None and name != "embed_tokens":
+            # The target lm_head lives on the last PP stage and can still
+            # be aliased; only the embedding needs its own copy.
+            continue
+        with torch.device(weight.device):
+            layer = layer_cls(target_config.vocab_size, target_config.hidden_size, params_dtype=weight.dtype)
+        load_quarot_target_layer(layer, vllm_config.model_config.model, weight_names, rotation, f"draft {name}.weight")
+        layer.quant_method.process_weights_after_loading(layer)
+        setattr(owner, name, layer)
+        setattr(model, own_flag, True)

[CI] Add slipcover for UT coverage checking (#20583)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Adds an incremental UT coverage gate and PR-comment coverage reporting
to the CI pipeline, and fixes 17 test cases that fail under parallel
`pytest-xdist` execution.

- Fixes: #20581 

Two commits:

- `[CI] Add slipcover for UT coverage checking` (`cdccf7e12`) —
slipcover + pytest-xdist + diff-cover collection, an 80% new-line
coverage gate on `cpu-ut`, and a single coverage-comment poster that
also works for fork PRs (`.github/workflows`, +238/-2).
- `[CI] Fix parallel test UT case failures` (`70d47e0e1`) — hardens
tests that depend on worker-local state, fixed ports, or tight timing
against parallel xdist scheduling (17 files, +210/-44).

**Coverage collection (slipcover + pytest-xdist, cpu only)**

- Installs `slipcover>=1.0.18`, `pytest-xdist`, and `diff-cover` in the
cpu-ut environment (`.github/workflows/_selected_tests.yaml`).
- Replaces the plain `pytest -sv` in the default UT path
(`.github/workflows/scripts/run_selected_tests.sh`, both single-target
and batch modes) with:
  ```bash
  python -m slipcover --source="${project_root}/vllm_ascend" \
--omit="*/tests/*" --json --out "${project_root}/tests/coverage.json" \
    -m pytest -n auto -sv --color=yes <targets...>
  ```
- slipcover: near-zero-overhead measurement (~5% vs ~180% median for
traditional coverage.py);
- `-n auto`: parallel execution across the runner's CPU cores; slipcover
(≥1.0.18) automatically merges coverage data from all xdist workers;
- the CLI rejects `--json` and `--xml` together, so the run emits JSON
only, and a follow-up step converts it to Cobertura XML (`python -m
slipcover --merge ./tests/coverage.json --xml --out
./tests/coverage.xml`).
- NPU targets keep plain `pytest` — on NPU runners each xdist worker
initializes torch_npu plus an engine subprocess, which crashed the
shared runner (run 111649013424: 22/22 e2e jobs failed with no
test-level errors) and contended for card memory (17/24 e2e jobs
failed). NPU e2e targets run serially; cpu keeps `-n auto`. The coverage
steps are guarded by `matrix.group.npu_type == 'cpu'` because NPU jobs
never produce `coverage.json`.

**Incremental coverage gate (diff-cover)**

After the test run, the reusable workflow runs `diff-cover` twice:

1. without a threshold, generating `tests/diff_coverage.md` — the report
always exists and is uploaded (`if: !cancelled()`), so the comment is
posted even when coverage is below the threshold;
2. with `--fail-under=80` against `origin/${{ github.base_ref }}` —
enforcing the gate separately so below-threshold coverage still fails
the job (and therefore `ci-gate`).

**Coverage report presentation (PR comment, fork-safe)**

- The markdown report is uploaded as the `coverage-report` artifact
(`if: !cancelled()`).
- A fork PR's `pull_request` GITHUB_TOKEN is read-only, so all comment
posting lives in the new `post_fork_coverage_comment.yaml` with
`pull-requests: write`:
- `workflow_run` (E2E completed) is the main trigger — it fires on any
completed run, green or not, so a failing coverage gate still gets its
report commented;
- `pull_request_target` (opened/synchronize) covers runs that finished
before the PR was opened;
- the PR number for forks travels via the `pr-context` artifact (new
`upload-pr-context` job in `pr_test.yaml`, `if: !cancelled()`) because
`workflow_run` payloads carry an empty `pull_requests[]` for fork PRs;
- security: the workflow never checks out or executes the fork's code —
it only downloads artifacts from the trusted `pr_test.yaml` run;
`comment_tag` keeps updating the same comment.
- Both workflows run on `linux-amd64-cpu-8-hk`: this org has no
GitHub-hosted runners, so `ubuntu-latest` would queue forever.
- Known limitation: `workflow_run`-triggered workflows run the default
branch's copy of the file, so that path activates after merge; during
the PR lifetime the `pull_request_target` path covers it.

**Parallel-UT hardening (17 files, fixes grouped by root cause)**

Today's UT only verifies pass/fail — a PR can merge new code with zero
test coverage. Running the cpu suite in parallel (`-n auto`) then
surfaced pre-existing worker-local state, fixed ports, and tight timing
assumptions:

1. **xdist worker global state**: snapshot/restore `_ASCEND_CONFIG` in
`test_linear` (a MagicMock leak broke 22 downstream cases via
`FileExistsError`); re-`importlib.reload` the platform module after the
patched reload in `test_platform` (by-value imports stay rebound to
mocks); register built-in KV-cache specs first in
`test_glm5next_kv_cache`; pin the uninitialized-config branch in
`test_moe_mlp`; mock `get_current_vllm_config` in `test_mla_v1` like the
sibling test class.
2. **Fixed-port collisions**: per-worker `MASTER_PORT` offsets in 4 e2e
compile tests (`EADDRINUSE`), per-worker port offsets in
`test_load_balance_proxy_server` (`PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER` gwN, 100-port
step).
3. **Timing**: relaxed subprocess/thread budgets
(`test_build_cache_concurrency`, `test_mooncake_hybrid`, rfork
session-server seed timeout 3s→30s incl. an EBADF mid-startup case); a
gate latch in `test_bus_worker` for determinism; tolerance for the lazy
`status_counter` assignment window in
`tools/profiling/aisbench_request_marker.py`.
4. **Upstream churn and numerics**: `enable_pcp` → `is_pcp_enabled`
(#19334) in `test_deepseek_v41_dspark`, `enable_dcp` → `is_dcp_enabled`
in `test_mla_v1`, and 2e-3 rtol/atol for the kimi dflash rope-cache
comparison in `test_patch_speculative_config_dflash` (CI fp32 kernels
drift by a couple of ulps; a semantic divergence such as a wrong mscale
moves values ~30% and still fails comfortably).

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. CI/workflow and test-only changes; no API, interface, or runtime
behavior change for vllm-ascend users. No release note fragment.

### How was this patch tested?

- **cpu-ut + E2E CI**: 11 rounds on the branch during development
(cpu-ut matrix: vLLM main commit and release tag). The failures observed
in those runs are exactly the ones fixed by the 17-file commit — e.g.
`EADDRINUSE` port collisions in the e2e compile tests, the
`FileExistsError` cascade from the `_ASCEND_CONFIG` MagicMock leak
(cpu-ut 1031-9), and the xdist worker-crash storms on NPU runners (run
111649013424).
- **Coverage format fix**: the `--json`/`--xml` mutual exclusion was
reproduced in CI, then fixed by splitting into a JSON-only run plus a
`slipcover --merge` XML conversion.
- **Incremental gate**: verified that below-threshold coverage fails the
job (and `ci-gate`) while the report artifact is still uploaded (`if:
!cancelled()`) and the comment is still posted (the poster fires on any
completed run).
- **PR comment posting**: verified for same-repo PRs and fork PRs — the
fork chain was exercised end-to-end via the `pr-context` artifact
bridge, without ever executing fork code.
- **Existing coverage path untouched**: the `enable-coverage` + OBS
upload loop is not modified by this PR; slipcover only replaces the
default (else-branch) pytest invocation.

#### Run selected tests — Full Comparison (All Scenarios)

> Step "Run selected tests without device" duration (wall time between
consecutive step markers), all 16 runs across every scenario.

| Scenario | main | 0.30 |
|---|---|---|
| no-cov (baseline) | 306.6s (5m06.6s) | 306.6s (5m06.6s) |
| coverage.py | 556.0s (9m16.0s) | 525.3s (8m45.3s) |
| slipcover (serial) | 536.3s (8m56.3s) | 541.5s (9m01.5s) |
| slipcover+1 | 553.1s (9m13.1s) | 567.3s (9m27.3s) |
| slipcover+2 | 467.7s (7m47.7s) | 459.6s (7m39.6s) |
| slipcover+4 | 470.8s (7m50.8s) | 457.0s (7m37.0s) |
| slipcover+8 | **413.3s (6m53.3s)** | **431.1s (7m11.1s)** |
| slipcover+16 | 506.6s (8m26.6s) | 525.6s (8m45.6s) |

Notes:

- `no-cov` runs the test suite once (`pytest -sv`); `coverage.py` wraps
the single pass with `coverage run`; `slipcover` scenarios run the suite
twice (plain `pytest` + slipcover collection), with `slipcover+N` adding
pytest-xdist `-n N` to the collection pass.
- Best overall: **slipcover+8** (413.3s / 431.1s) — the only two-pass
configuration that beats serial slipcover and approaches `coverage.py`
cost while producing real coverage artifacts; `slipcover+16` regresses
due to 16 workers oversubscribing the 8-core runner.
- main vs 0.30 differences are within runner noise (±30s) except under
`coverage.py` tracing, where the interaction of tracing overhead with
the vLLM version adds ~30s.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [ ] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: N/A — CI workflow and test-only
change; no product code touched.
- [ ] **Regression test**: N/A — no product-code bug fix; CI workflows
are verified by running them.
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: exercised in CI — gate failure
(report artifact still uploaded, comment still posted), fork-PR
read-only token (handled by the dedicated poster workflow), and missing
`diff_coverage.md` (warning + skip) paths.
- [ ] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: no new unit tests added; the 17
changed test files make existing tests reliable under parallel xdist
execution.
- [x] **Performance impact**: slipcover (~5% overhead) + `-n auto`
parallelism replaces the serial plain-pytest run in the default cpu-ut
path.

+      - name: Generate Cobertura XML from coverage data
+        # tests/coverage.json is only produced by the slipcover pytest runs,
+        # which run on cpu only (NPU targets run plain pytest, see
+        # run_selected_tests.sh); without the guard this step fails on every

+        if: ${{ matrix.group.npu_type == 'cpu' && inputs.enable-coverage != true }}
+        run: |
+          python -m slipcover --merge ./tests/coverage.json \
+            --xml --out ./tests/coverage.xml
+
+      - name: Generate coverage comment on summary
+        # Depends on coverage.xml generated by the step above (cpu only, and
+        # only when enable-coverage != true, which keeps the diff-cover trio
+        # out of the legacy coverage.py + OBS path).
+        if: ${{ matrix.group.npu_type == 'cpu' && inputs.enable-coverage != true }}
+        run: |
+          diff-cover ./tests/coverage.xml --compare-branch=origin/${{ github.base_ref }} \
+            --markdown-report ./tests/diff_coverage.md
+          cat ./tests/diff_coverage.md >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY}"
+
+      - name: Generate PR coverage comment
+        if: ${{ matrix.group.npu_type == 'cpu' && inputs.enable-coverage != true }}
+        run: |
+           python3 .github/workflows/scripts/coverage_comment.py \
+            --input ./tests/diff_coverage.md \
+            --output ./tests/coverage_comment.md \
+            --summary-url "${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}"
+
+      - name: Upload diff coverage report
+        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
+        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: coverage-report
+          path: |
+            ./tests/diff_coverage.md
+            ./tests/coverage_comment.md
+          if-no-files-found: ignore
+
       - name: Upload coverage data
         if: ${{ !cancelled() && inputs.enable-coverage }}
         continue-on-error: true

+#   it travels in the pr-context artifact uploaded by the E2E run's

+# - pull_request_target (opened/synchronize) covers the rare case where a
+#   run for the head sha already exists when the PR is opened or re-opened.
+#   The run does not need to be green: cpu-ut uploads the coverage-report
+#   artifact even on failed runs, so the latest run is used regardless of
+#   its conclusion. Without the workflow_run trigger, a fork PR would never
+#   get its comment, because this event fires at push time, before a run for
+#   the new head sha can exist.

+    # failed e2e matrix does not block the comment as long as cpu-ut

+"""Generate a compact PR comment from diff-cover output.
+
+diff-cover produces a markdown report like:
+
+    # Diff Coverage
+    ## Diff: origin/main...HEAD, staged and unstaged changes
+
+    - vllm_ascend/foo.py (50.0%): Missing lines 10-12
+
+    ## Summary
+
+    - **Total**: 20 lines
+    - **Missing**: 10 lines
+    - **Coverage**: 50%
+
+    ## vllm_ascend/foo.py
+    ...
+
+This script extracts the H1 title and the three summary bullet points
+(Total, Missing, Coverage) and writes them to the output file as a
+compact PR comment.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+def extract_lines(markdown: str) -> list[str]:
+    """Extract the H1 title and the Summary section bullet points.
+
+    Returns a list of lines in the order: title, total, missing, coverage.
+    """
+    title = None
+    summary_bullets = []
+
+    in_summary = False
+    for line in markdown.splitlines():
+        stripped = line.strip()
+
+        # Capture the top-level title (# Diff Coverage)
+        if title is None and stripped.startswith("# ") and not stripped.startswith("## "):
+            title = stripped
+            continue
+
+        # Enter the Summary section
+        if stripped.startswith("## Summary"):
+            in_summary = True
+            continue
+
+        # Once in Summary, collect bullet lines until next heading
+        if in_summary:
+            if stripped.startswith("#"):
+                break
+            if stripped.startswith("- **"):
+                summary_bullets.append(stripped)
+
+    return [line for line in (title,) + tuple(summary_bullets) if line is not None]
+
+
+def build_comment(lines: list[str], summary_url: str = "") -> str:
+    """Render the extracted lines as a markdown PR comment."""
+    if not lines:
+        return "## Diff Coverage\n\nNo coverage data found.\n"
+    out = "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
+    if summary_url:
+        out += f"\nMore info see: [Summary]({summary_url})\n"
+    return out
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--input", required=True, help="Path to diff_coverage.md")
+    parser.add_argument("--output", required=True, help="Path to write coverage_comment.md")
+    parser.add_argument("--summary-url", default="", help="URL to the cpu-ut job execution page")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+
+    in_path = Path(args.input)
+    if not in_path.exists():
+        print(f"::warning::input file {in_path} not found; no coverage comment generated", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 0
+
+    markdown = in_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+    lines = extract_lines(markdown)
+    comment = build_comment(lines, args.summary_url)
+
+    out_path = Path(args.output)
+    out_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    out_path.write_text(comment, encoding="utf-8")
+    print(f"Wrote {out_path} ({len(lines)} lines)")
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())
