+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM Ascend project
+
+"""Experimental M3.1 Flash DSpark adapter using the existing Ascend protocol.
+
+Only draft model differences are implemented here: Flash norms, MLP, the
+standalone-checkpoint configuration contract and native BF16/MXFP8 weight
+mapping. Target verification, Markov drafting, confidence, batching and
+cache metadata use the supplied vLLM/vLLM-Ascend implementations unchanged.
+
+``SpeculativeConfig.hf_config_override`` routes the draft checkpoint's
+config through ``draft_hf_override``. The draft geometry comes from the
+checkpoint's own ``dspark/config.json``; ``draft_config_from_file`` only
+adds the aliases the DSpark stack reads and corrects the export's
+target-model leftovers.
+"""
+
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import regex as re
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+from torch import nn
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.layernorm import GemmaRMSNorm, RMSNorm
+from vllm.model_executor.models.qwen3_dflash import (
+    DFlashQwen3Attention,
+    DFlashQwen3DecoderLayer,
+    DFlashQwen3ForCausalLM,
+    _resolve_layer_attention,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.models.qwen3_dspark import Qwen3DSparkModel
+
+from vllm_ascend.models.minimax_m3.minimax_m3 import MiniMaxM3MLP
+from vllm_ascend.models.qwen3_dspark import AscendQwen3DSparkForCausalLM
+
+PREFIX = "language_model.model.dspark."
+ADAPTER_ARCHITECTURE = "DSparkMiniMaxDraftModel"
+MAX_SAFETENSORS_HEADER_BYTES = 10 * 1024 * 1024
+MXFP8_GROUP_SIZE = 32
+
+_MXFP8_PROJECTIONS = (
+    "self_attn.q_proj",
+    "self_attn.k_proj",
+    "self_attn.v_proj",
+    "self_attn.qkv_proj",
+    "self_attn.o_proj",
+    "mlp.gate_proj",
+    "mlp.up_proj",
+    "mlp.gate_up_proj",
+    "mlp.down_proj",
+)
+
+
+def map_weight_name(name):
+    if not name.startswith(PREFIX):
+        raise ValueError(f"Unexpected tensor outside standalone DSpark: {name}")
+    name = name[len(PREFIX) :]
+    name = re.sub(r"^(layers\.\d+)\.decoder_layer\.", r"\1.", name)
+    if name.startswith("final_norm."):
+        name = "norm." + name[len("final_norm.") :]
+    return name
+
+
+def expected_shapes(config):
+    h = config["hidden_size"]
+    hd = config["head_dim"]
+    q = config["num_attention_heads"] * hd
+    kv = config["num_key_value_heads"] * hd
+    ffn = config["dspark_ffn_hidden_size"]
+    n = config["num_hidden_layers"]
+    vocab = config["vocab_size"]
+    rank = config["dspark_markov_rank"]
+    shapes = {
+        "fc.weight": [h, h * len(config["dspark_target_layer_ids"])],
+        "hidden_norm.weight": [h],
+        "norm.weight": [h],
+        "markov_head.markov_w1.weight": [vocab, rank],
+        "markov_head.markov_w2.weight": [vocab, rank],
+        "confidence_head.proj.weight": [1, h + rank],
+        "confidence_head.proj.bias": [1],
+    }
+    for i in range(n):
+        p = f"layers.{i}."
+        for norm in ("input_layernorm", "post_attention_layernorm"):
+            shapes[p + norm + ".weight"] = [h]
+        for norm in ("q_norm", "k_norm"):
+            shapes[p + "self_attn." + norm + ".weight"] = [hd]
+        matrices = {
+            "self_attn.q_proj": [q, h],
+            "self_attn.k_proj": [kv, h],
+            "self_attn.v_proj": [kv, h],
+            "self_attn.o_proj": [h, q],
+            "mlp.gate_proj": [ffn, h],
+            "mlp.up_proj": [ffn, h],
+            "mlp.down_proj": [h, ffn],
+        }
+        for name, shape in matrices.items():
+            shapes[p + name + ".weight"] = shape
+    return shapes
+
+
+def validate_header(header, config):
+    expected = expected_shapes(config)
+    mapped = {}
+    for name, info in header.items():
+        if name == "__metadata__":
+            continue
+        mapped_name = map_weight_name(name)
+        if mapped_name in mapped:
+            raise ValueError(f"Duplicate mapped tensor: {mapped_name}")
+        mapped[mapped_name] = info
+    uses_mxfp8 = any(info["dtype"] == "F8_E4M3" for info in mapped.values())
+    quantized = {name: shape for name, shape in expected.items() if name.startswith("layers.") and len(shape) == 2}
+    scales = (
+        {
+            name.removesuffix("weight") + "weight_scale_inv": [
+                shape[0],
+                (shape[1] + MXFP8_GROUP_SIZE - 1) // MXFP8_GROUP_SIZE,
+            ]
+            for name, shape in quantized.items()
+        }
+        if uses_mxfp8
+        else {}
+    )
+    schema = set(expected) | set(scales)
+    if set(mapped) != schema:
+        raise ValueError(f"Tensor schema mismatch: missing={schema - set(mapped)}, extra={set(mapped) - schema}")
+    for name, shape in {**expected, **scales}.items():
+        if list(mapped[name]["shape"]) != shape:
+            raise ValueError(f"Tensor shape mismatch: {name}, {mapped[name]['shape']} != {shape}")
+        dtype = mapped[name]["dtype"]
+        expected_dtype = "U8" if name in scales else "F8_E4M3" if uses_mxfp8 and name in quantized else "BF16"
+        if dtype != expected_dtype:
+            raise ValueError(f"Expected native {expected_dtype} DSpark tensor, got {name}: {dtype}")
+    return mapped
+
+
+def iter_draft_weights(weights, config):
+    # Keep header-only configuration preparation independent of Torch imports.
+    import torch
+
+    tensors = {}
+    for name, value in weights:
+        if name in tensors:
+            raise ValueError(f"Duplicate input tensor: {name}")
+        tensors[name] = value
+    header = {}
+    for name, value in tensors.items():
+        header[name] = {
+            "shape": list(value.shape),
+            "dtype": {torch.bfloat16: "BF16", torch.float8_e4m3fn: "F8_E4M3", torch.uint8: "U8"}.get(
+                value.dtype, str(value.dtype)
+            ),
+        }
+    validate_header(header, config)
+    for name, value in tensors.items():
+        yield map_weight_name(name).replace("weight_scale_inv", "weight_scale"), value
+
+
+def read_draft_header(model_root):
+    """Read draft metadata without loading or converting weight tensors."""
+    draft = Path(model_root) / "dspark"
+    shards = sorted(draft.glob("*.safetensors"))
+    if not shards:
+        raise ValueError(f"MiniMax DSpark weights are missing from {draft}")
+    header = {}
+    for shard in shards:
+        with shard.open("rb") as stream:
+            size = int.from_bytes(stream.read(8), "little")
+            if not 0 < size < MAX_SAFETENSORS_HEADER_BYTES:
+                raise ValueError(f"Invalid DSpark safetensors header size: {shard}")
+            metadata = json.loads(stream.read(size))
+        for name, info in metadata.items():
+            if name == "__metadata__":
+                continue
+            if name in header:
+                raise ValueError(f"Duplicate DSpark tensor across shards: {name}")
+            header[name] = info
+    return header
+
+
+def draft_config_from_file(source, header):
+    """Normalize the checkpoint's ``dspark/config.json`` for the Ascend stack.
+
+    The draft geometry comes from the file itself. What remains here is the
+    contract the DSpark speculator and this adapter read: alias names, norm
+    defaults and corrections for the target-model leftovers every known export
+    carries in its dense draft (MoE routing and FFN width). The export's own
+    ``quantization_config`` describes the ModelSlim calibration, so MXFP8
+    ascend sections are derived from the tensor header instead.
+    """
+    draft = source.get("text_config", source)
+    architectures = source.get("architectures") or draft.get("architectures") or []
+    if ADAPTER_ARCHITECTURE not in architectures:
+        raise ValueError("Expected a MiniMax DSpark draft config, not a target model config")
+    block_size = draft["dspark_block_size"]
+    noise_token = draft["dspark_noise_token_id"]
+    config = dict(draft)
+    config.update(
+        {
+            "architectures": [ADAPTER_ARCHITECTURE],
+            "model_type": "minimax_m3_text",
+            # Aliases the upstream DSpark speculator reads.
+            "n_predict": block_size,
+            "target_layer_ids": list(draft["dspark_target_layer_ids"]),
+            "markov_rank": draft.get("markov_rank", draft["dspark_markov_rank"]),
+            "markov_head_type": draft.get("markov_head_type", draft.get("dspark_markov_head_type", "vanilla")),
+            "dspark_markov_head_type": draft.get("dspark_markov_head_type", "vanilla"),
+            "mask_token_id": noise_token,
+            "ptd_token_id": noise_token,
+            "draft_vocab_size": draft["vocab_size"],
+            # Norm types and confidence flags the adapter requires.
+            "dspark_hidden_norm_type": draft.get("dspark_hidden_norm_type", "gemma"),
+            "dspark_final_norm_type": draft.get("dspark_final_norm_type", "gemma"),
+            "enable_confidence_head": draft.get("enable_confidence_head", True),
+            "confidence_head_with_markov": draft.get("confidence_head_with_markov", True),
+            "use_aux_hidden_state": True,
+            "sample_from_anchor": True,
+            # Every known export copies the target's MoE routing and FFN width
+            # into the dense draft; keep the draft dense.
+            "intermediate_size": draft["dspark_ffn_hidden_size"],
+            "num_local_experts": 0,
+            "num_experts_per_tok": 0,
+            "n_shared_experts": 0,
+            "sparse_attention_config": None,
+            "rope_parameters": draft.get("rope_parameters")
+            or {
+                "rope_type": "default",
+                "rope_theta": draft["rope_theta"],
+                "partial_rotary_factor": draft.get("partial_rotary_factor", draft["rotary_dim"] / draft["head_dim"]),
+            },
+        }
+    )
+    config.pop("quantization_config", None)
+    mapped = validate_header(header, config)
+    if any(info["dtype"] == "F8_E4M3" for info in mapped.values()):
+        target_layers = (draft.get("dflash_config") or {}).get("num_target_layers")
+        if not isinstance(target_layers, int):
+            raise ValueError("MXFP8 DSpark exports must declare dflash_config.num_target_layers")
+        quant = {"quant_method": "ascend", "group_size": MXFP8_GROUP_SIZE}
+        # DFlash offsets runtime attention names past the target's layers.
+        for layer in range(draft["num_hidden_layers"]):
+            for projection in _MXFP8_PROJECTIONS:
+                quant[f"model.layers.{target_layers + layer}.{projection}.weight"] = "W8A8_MXFP8"
+        config["quantization_config"] = quant
+    return config
+
+
+def draft_hf_override(hf_config):
+    # Called through SpeculativeConfig.hf_config_override once the draft
+    # ModelConfig is built from the standalone checkpoint under
+    # ``<model_root>/dspark``: the loaded config's ``_name_or_path`` is that
+    # draft directory, so the checkpoint stays the source of truth. A
+    # module-level callable remains picklable for workers.
+    # HFConfigParser probes callables with an empty sentinel config before
+    # loading the real checkpoint. Preserve its source config class selection.
+    if hf_config.model_type.startswith("dummy_"):
+        return hf_config
+    from vllm.transformers_utils.configs.minimax_m3 import MiniMaxM3TextConfig
+
+    model_root = Path(hf_config._name_or_path).parent
+    config = draft_config_from_file(hf_config.to_dict(), read_draft_header(model_root))
+    return MiniMaxM3TextConfig(**config)
+
+
+class MiniMaxFlashDraftLayer(DFlashQwen3DecoderLayer):
+    def __init__(self, vllm_config, *, config, layer_idx, cache_config=None, quant_config=None, prefix=""):
+        nn.Module.__init__(self)
+        self.hidden_size = config.hidden_size
+        sliding_window, causal = _resolve_layer_attention(config, layer_idx)
+        self.self_attn = DFlashQwen3Attention(
+            hidden_size=config.hidden_size,
+            num_heads=config.num_attention_heads,
+            num_kv_heads=config.num_key_value_heads,
+            rope_parameters=dict(config.rope_parameters),
+            max_position=config.max_position_embeddings,
+            head_dim=config.head_dim,
+            rms_norm_eps=config.rms_norm_eps,
+            attention_bias=False,
+            sliding_window=sliding_window,
+            causal=causal,
+            is_neox_style=True,
+            cache_config=cache_config,
+            quant_config=quant_config,
+            prefix=f"{prefix}.self_attn",
+        )
+        self.self_attn.q_norm = GemmaRMSNorm(config.head_dim, eps=config.rms_norm_eps)
+        self.self_attn.k_norm = GemmaRMSNorm(config.head_dim, eps=config.rms_norm_eps)
+        self.mlp = MiniMaxM3MLP(
+            config,
+            intermediate_size=config.dspark_ffn_hidden_size,
+            quant_config=quant_config,
+            prefix=f"{prefix}.mlp",
+        )
+        self.input_layernorm = GemmaRMSNorm(config.hidden_size, eps=config.rms_norm_eps)
+        self.post_attention_layernorm = GemmaRMSNorm(config.hidden_size, eps=config.rms_norm_eps)
+
+
+class MiniMaxFlashDSparkModel(Qwen3DSparkModel):
+    decoder_layer_cls = MiniMaxFlashDraftLayer
+
+    def __init__(self, **kwargs):
+        super().__init__(**kwargs)
+        config = self.config
+        for name, choice in (("hidden_norm", config.dspark_hidden_norm_type), ("norm", config.dspark_final_norm_type)):
+            if choice not in ("rms", "gemma"):

[Doc][Feature] Add Triton contribution and Ascend JIT warmup guides (#21201)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Add two English developer guides with navigation entries and
cross-links. The operator guidelines appear last under Developer Guide >
Contribution; the warmup guide appears under Developer Guide > Design
Documents:

- **Contributing Triton operators:** a deliverables checklist followed
by functionality, accuracy, performance, and clean-code requirements.
Appendices define accuracy tolerances and summarize JIT specialization
and recompilation.
- **Triton JIT warmup on Ascend:** the vLLM registry and vLLM-Ascend
integration, startup order, wrapper and registration steps, a Q-RMS
example, validation, and configuration. It references the upstream
warmup guide for shared framework details.

The contribution criteria are proposed for maintainer review. Chinese
translation files are not included.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No runtime behavior changes. The developer documentation gains
contribution and warmup integration guidance. A documentation release
note is included in `release_notes/fragments/21201.yaml`.

### How was this patch tested?

- Passed markdownlint-cli 0.45.0 with the repository configuration for
both guides and the developer index.
- Passed `git diff --check`.
- Checked the warmup description against vLLM and vLLM-Ascend source,
including the registry, Triton helper, worker startup, Ascend wrapper,
Q-RMS registration, and warmup tests.
- Local English/Chinese translation consistency checks passed;
translation artifacts remain outside this PR.
- Full local formatting checks were blocked by missing `pre-commit`; the
local link checker was blocked by certificate-chain verification. The
full MkDocs build and link checks remain for CI.
- Runtime and device tests were not run because this PR changes
documentation only.

### Checklist

Runtime boundary, regression, error-path, and performance tests are not
applicable to this documentation-only change. Required CI checks should
pass before merge.

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/ba15685ab7f4f5fbed8630bbb7441f8837e76fbe

+# Triton JIT warmup on Ascend
+
+This guide describes how to register and precompile Triton kernels during vLLM-Ascend startup. Use it with the upstream [JIT Kernel Warmup guide](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/contributing/jit_kernel_warmup/) and the [vLLM revision verified by the target branch](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/main/.github/vllm-main-verified.commit).
+
+## Integration mechanism
+
+| Component | Responsibility |
+| --- | --- |
+| vLLM `JitWarmupRegistry` | Collect registrations, expand compile keys and deduplicate them per wrapper. |
+| vLLM Triton helper | Reuse the launch specification for warmup compilation and runtime execution. |
+| Ascend runner | Activate the registry during component initialization. |
+| `AscendTritonJitKernel` | Adapt the parallel-compilation gate for CANN. |
+| Ascend `kernel_warmup()` | Complete late registration, retain Ascend wrappers and invoke registry warmup. |
+
+Register an `AscendTritonJitKernel` instance inside the runner's active window. Registration outside a window is a no-op; the current orchestrator removes instances that do not derive from the Ascend base.
+
+## Startup and execution flow
+
+1. **Initialize and register.** The runner activates its `jit_warmup_registry` while constructing selected components. Their `register_warmup(...)` calls record the wrapper and configuration; registration itself does not compile kernels.
+2. **Run configured dummy inputs.** The [worker](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/main/vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py) runs the configured model dummy inputs. These executions can already trigger Triton compilation.
+3. **Complete registration.** The worker calls [kernel_warmup(worker)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/main/vllm_ascend/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py). It adds registrations that need final runtime metadata and removes wrappers that cannot compile through the Ascend base.
+4. **Compile required variants.** `registry.warmup()` expands registered configurations through `get_warmup_keys`, deduplicates keys per wrapper and compiles each required variant. For a non-autotuned wrapper, the path is `compile → warmup_inputs → __call__ → launch → kernel.warmup`; it compiles without executing the kernel.
+5. **Capture and serve.** The worker captures graphs when enabled. Runtime wrapper calls use real tensors and the actual grid; Triton reuses matching cached artifacts. A variant not covered by warmup can still compile on first use.
+
+`CompileKey` deduplicates warmup work; it does not replace Triton's runtime specialization and cache keys.
+
+## Integration steps
+
+### 1. Define the warmup domain
+
+List the supported dtypes, constexpr values, scalar specialization classes, layouts and compilation options. Generate keys for reachable variants, including applicable out-of-graph paths. See [JIT specialization and recompilation](../contribution/triton_operators.md#jit-specialization-and-recompilation).
+
+### 2. Implement the Ascend wrapper
+
+Derive the wrapper from [AscendTritonJitKernel](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/main/vllm_ascend/ops/triton/ascend_jit_warmup.py). For an explicit-key wrapper, implement:
+
+| Member | Requirement |
+| --- | --- |
+| `kernel` | Reference the JIT kernel. |
+| `CompileKey` | A hashable key identifying a required variant. |
+| `dispatch` | Map concrete dispatch inputs to a key. |
+| `get_warmup_keys` | Generate keys from the supported configuration domain. |
+| `warmup_inputs` | Supply every required `__call__` argument, including launch-only arguments. |
+| `__call__` | Use `@kernel_launcher`; return the grid and launch arguments. |
+
+Use `TritonWarmupTensor` for compile-only tensor metadata. Match runtime dtype, strides, alignment and scalar specialization. Keep operations that require tensor contents outside this path.
+
+### 3. Connect runtime calls
+
+Create one wrapper instance for registration and execution. In the public operator function, replace direct kernel launch with the wrapper call. Preserve output allocation, grid dimensions, argument binding and return values.
+
+### 4. Register in the selected component
+
+Place `register_warmup(...)` in the initialization path of the component that selects and uses the operator. Pass the configuration expected by the wrapper's `get_warmup_keys`.
+
+| Operator owner | Where to register or integrate | Source reference |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Model | Register in the model layer's `__init__`, while the runner constructs the model inside its registry window. | `DeepseekV41Indexer.__init__` registers indexer kernels in [indexer.py](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/main/vllm_ascend/models/deepseek_v41/indexer.py). |
+| Attention | Register in the selected metadata builder's `__init__`. If keys need allocated cache layouts, register after allocation in the runner's cache initialization window. | `AscendDSAMetadataBuilder.__init__` in [dsa_v1.py](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/main/vllm_ascend/attention/dsa_v1.py); `initialize_kv_cache` in the [runner](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/main/vllm_ascend/worker/v2/model_runner.py). |
+| Sampling | When adding an Ascend sampling wrapper, register it during initialization of the selected sampling component, inside the runner registry window. | Use the [runner](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/main/vllm_ascend/worker/v2/model_runner.py) that constructs the component; the former v1 sampling registration helper has been removed. |
+| Worker / runner | Own registry windows and compilation timing. For keys requiring final component or input-batch metadata, call a late-registration helper before `registry.warmup()`. | `_register_dspark_swa_indices_warmup` and `kernel_warmup` in [kernel_warmup.py](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/main/vllm_ascend/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py). |
+| Compilation pass | If a pass introduces a wrapped Triton operator, provide its key domain through an initialization or late-registration path above, once its configuration is known. A graph rewrite alone does not register the wrapper. | Follow the wrapper and registration steps in this guide; the current Ascend compilation directory has no dedicated `register_warmup` entry point. |
+| Runtime | Call the same wrapper instance with real tensors. Register variants before serving; a runtime call alone does not populate the warmup registry. | `triton_q_rms` in [rms_norm.py](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/main/vllm_ascend/ops/triton/rms_norm.py). |
+
+For the Q-RMS path, the runner's `_initialize_kv_cache_upstream` activates the registry around the upstream cache initialization that constructs attention metadata builders. The builder then registers the same wrapper instance used by `triton_q_rms`.
+
+For a new initialization path, check that the caller encloses component construction in `with runner.jit_warmup_registry.activate():`. If it does not, add the window at the runner call site using its existing registry. A late-registration helper must also activate that same registry. Registration outside a window is a no-op; importing a wrapper alone does not register it.
+
+Ordinary component registration does not require adding the operator to a central list or calling `registry.warmup()` from the component. The worker owns compilation timing.
+
+## Example: Q-RMS
+
+The existing [Q-RMS implementation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/main/vllm_ascend/ops/triton/rms_norm.py) shows the complete wrapper and runtime call:
+
+1. `TritonQRmsKernel.CompileKey` contains `dim`, `block_m` and `dtype`.
+2. `get_warmup_keys` enumerates reachable power-of-two `block_m` values up to the UB-derived bound.
+3. `warmup_inputs` supplies tensor metadata and all launcher arguments, including `num_vectorcore`.
+4. `triton_q_rms` calculates the runtime tile, allocates the output and calls `_TRITON_Q_RMS_KERNEL`.
+
+[AscendDSAMetadataBuilder](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/main/vllm_ascend/attention/dsa_v1.py) registers that instance during construction:
+
+```python
+from vllm_ascend.ops.triton.rms_norm import _TRITON_Q_RMS_KERNEL
+
+_TRITON_Q_RMS_KERNEL.register_warmup(vllm_config)
+```
+
+## Validation
+
+- Verify expected keys for supported configurations and specialization boundaries.
+- Verify registration inside the runner window and no registration outside it.
+- Verify warmup argument binding and unchanged runtime output after wrapper migration.
+- On the target device, test cold and warm caches; record compilation separately for dummy runs, explicit warmup, graph capture and serving.
+
+Add tests under `tests/ut/model_executor/warmup/`. Refer to [test_jit_warmup_rms.py](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/main/tests/ut/model_executor/warmup/test_jit_warmup_rms.py) for keys and registration, and [test_kernel_warmup.py](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/main/tests/ut/model_executor/warmup/test_kernel_warmup.py) for orchestration. In a prepared test environment, run:
+
+```bash
+python -m pytest tests/ut/model_executor/warmup/test_jit_warmup_rms.py tests/ut/model_executor/warmup/test_kernel_warmup.py -q
+```
+
+Mock tests validate registration and scheduling; use device tests for compilation coverage and numerical correctness.
+
+## Configuration and troubleshooting
+
+| Setting | Behavior |
+| --- | --- |
+| `kernel_config.enable_jit_warmup` | Enables registry warmup; defaults to `True`. |
+| `VLLM_TRITON_JIT_WARMUP_NUM_THREADS` | Defaults to `4`; set to `1` for serial compilation. |
+
+Parallel compilation requires `AsyncCompileMode` and a non-autotuned wrapper. Autotuning may execute kernels and requires suitable real inputs. `enforce_eager` does not globally disable registry warmup.
+
+| Symptom | Check |
+| --- | --- |
+| Empty registry | Component selection, active window and Ascend base class |
+| Warmup `TypeError` | Missing or mismatched `__call__` arguments |
+| Compilation during serving | Uncovered specialization classes or missing registration |
+| Incorrect runtime output | Grid, argument binding, masks and output writes |
+| Parallel compilation failure | Retry with one thread and check compiler compatibility |

+# Contributing Triton operators
+
+## Deliverables checklist
+
+- [ ] PR description.
+- [ ] Source files.
+- [ ] Markdown operator document: `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/docs/<operator>.md`.
+- [ ] Test files: `tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/`; warmup unit tests, when applicable: `tests/ut/model_executor/warmup/`.
+- [ ] Repository-wide deliverables: see the [contribution guide](https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/ascend/en/latest/developer_guide/contribution/index.html) and [release note guide](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/main/release_notes/README.md).
+
+## Overall objectives
+
+Triton operators merged into the project should meet quality requirements in four areas:
+
+1. **Functionality:** Implement the required functionality and preserve compatibility across applicable devices supported by the project.
+2. **Accuracy:** Meet operator-level and model-level accuracy criteria.
+3. **Performance:** Performance optimization PRs improve over the baseline. Other PRs avoid unjustified performance regressions.
+4. **Clean Code:** Keep code readable and maintainable, use reasonable specialization, and avoid undeclared external side effects.
+
+## Detailed requirements
+
+Contributors must provide the following content in the deliverables before merge.
+
+### Functionality
+
+- [ ] The PR description includes:
+    - [ ] Functionality, inputs and outputs, production callers, and whether the operator is framework-wide or model-specific.
+    - [ ] Motivation, such as model support, a bug fix, performance optimization, or temporary compatibility. Temporary implementations include a replacement and removal plan.
+    - [ ] Cross-device compatibility and actual validation results. Operators should not be restricted to one particular device; device-specific optimization preserves functionality and correctness on other applicable devices.
+- [ ] The Markdown document follows the [operator template](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/main/vllm_ascend/ops/triton/docs/triton_description_specification.md), describing functionality, algorithm, parameters, constraints, origin and differences, and test entry points.
+- [ ] The implementation matches the documented inputs, outputs, and behavior.
+- [ ] The operator is integrated into the corresponding model or shared operator call path in vLLM-Ascend.
+
+### Accuracy
+
+- [ ] The PR description includes:
+    - [ ] Operator accuracy results against a reference implementation.
+    - [ ] Model accuracy results against the baseline on an evaluation dataset such as GPQA, with evaluation settings.
+- [ ] Test files provide:
+    - [ ] Coverage of all declared input categories and relevant boundaries.
+    - [ ] For framework-wide operators, coverage of the general interface and representative real shapes from applicable models.
+    - [ ] For model-specific operators, coverage of real shapes and parameter combinations reachable in the target models under the declared configurations.
+    - [ ] Parameterized representative cases and boundaries, avoiding redundant cases.
+- [ ] The Markdown document identifies the reference implementation, applicable accuracy criteria, and test commands.
+
+See [Reference accuracy criteria](#reference-accuracy-criteria) in the appendix. Data movement and integer or index outputs require exact comparison as appropriate to their semantics.
+
+### Performance
+
+For non-performance PRs, avoid unjustified performance regressions. New functionality may justify a reasonable end-to-end regression; quantify and explain it. Model performance may be reported as percentage changes rather than absolute figures.
+
+- [ ] The PR description includes:
+    - [ ] Operator performance results against the baseline.
+    - [ ] Model performance results on a workload such as GSM8K, identifying latency or throughput metrics.
+    - [ ] Matching comparison conditions, including versions, devices, inputs, model configuration, and measurement methodology.
+
+### Clean Code
+
+- [ ] Source files meet these requirements:
+    - [ ] Clear responsibility boundaries, reasonable reuse, and comments explaining important design choices. See [coding guidelines](#triton-operator-coding-guidelines).
+    - [ ] Clear naming consistent with surrounding code. Operator documents are named after the operator and follow the [repository layout](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/main/vllm_ascend/ops/triton/README.md).
+    - [ ] No silent changes to caller-visible dtype, layout, contents, or external state. Permitted in-place behavior is documented and tested.
+- [ ] The PR description includes a recompilation risk assessment based on [JIT specialization and recompilation](#jit-specialization-and-recompilation):
+    - [ ] **White-box analysis:** Parameter domains, specialization triggers, and justification for annotations such as constexpr and specialization controls.
+    - [ ] **Black-box validation:** Observed shapes and specialization metadata on a workload such as GPQA, with compilation counts separated by startup and serving phases.
+    - [ ] Causes and mitigation of unnecessary variants, plus remaining compilation conditions.
+- [ ] Where warmup is used:
+    - [ ] Source files include the wrapper and registration site for required variants.
+    - [ ] Test files cover key space, registration windows, and runtime coverage.
+    - [ ] The Markdown document describes warmup scope and related configuration.
+
+Reduce unnecessary specialization before warming up required variants. See the upstream [vLLM JIT kernel warmup guide](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/contributing/jit_kernel_warmup/) for integration. For Ascend registration and validation, see [Triton JIT warmup on Ascend](../Design_Documents/triton_jit_warmup.md).
+
+## Appendix
+
+### Reference accuracy criteria
+
+- **Absolute tolerance (`atol`)**: a fixed error allowance, including when the reference is near zero.
+- **Relative tolerance (`rtol`)**: an error allowance proportional to the absolute reference value.
+
+Compare each output element `actual_i` with its reference `golden_i`:
+
+$$
+\left|\mathrm{actual}_i-\mathrm{golden}_i\right| \leq \mathrm{atol}+\mathrm{rtol}\cdot\left|\mathrm{golden}_i\right|
+$$
+
+| Output dtype | rtol | atol | Maximum absolute error |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| FP16 | $2^{-9}$ | $2^{-9}$ | 0.1 |
+| BF16 | $2^{-6}$ | $2^{-6}$ | 1 |
+| FP32 | $2^{-10}$ | $2^{-16}$ | 0.01 |
+
+Both conditions must hold:
+
+1. At least 99% of elements satisfy the combined tolerance.
+2. The maximum absolute error across all elements does not exceed the corresponding limit.
+
+The maximum-error rule is $\max\left(\mathrm{fixed\_limit},\;32\cdot\mathrm{ULP}_{1.0}\right)$, where $\mathrm{ULP}_{1.0}$ is the unit in the last place at 1.0 for the output dtype; use the explicit limits in the table.
+
+### Triton operator coding guidelines
+
+#### Naming
+
+- Use `snake_case` for functions, ordinary parameters, and local variables, for example `hidden_size` and `num_tokens`.
+- Use `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` for constants and compile-time parameters, for example `BLOCK_SIZE`. Use `tl.constexpr` only when compile-time evaluation is needed.
+- For Tensor arguments of a Triton kernel, prefer `xxx_ptr` names, for example `input_ptr` and `output_ptr`.
+- Replace unexplained magic numbers with named constants or derived expressions. Explain the purpose and selection rationale of algorithm and tuning constants.
+
+#### Public interface and integration
+
+- Expose a Python wrapper; callers use it instead of launching the kernel directly.
+- Encapsulate input handling, output allocation, grid calculation and tiling in the wrapper.
+- Document supported shapes, dtypes, layouts and in-place behavior. Reject unsupported inputs or use an existing fallback.
+- Use consistent launch-configuration rules for warmup and runtime execution.
+
+#### Interface structure example
+
+The following pseudocode shows the interface boundaries; it is not a runnable operator implementation.
+
+```python
+@triton.jit
+def _your_op_kernel(input_ptr, output_ptr, num_elements, BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr):
+    ...
+
+
+def your_op(input):
+    # Validate inputs and prepare the output.
+    ...
+    # Select tiling and calculate the grid internally.
+    ...
+    _your_op_kernel[grid](
+        input, output, num_elements, BLOCK_SIZE=block_size
+    )
+    return output
+```
+
+Callers import and use the public entry point:
+
+```python
+from path.to.your_op import your_op
+
+output = your_op(input)
+```
+
+### JIT specialization and recompilation
+
+A new specialization requires compilation when no reusable artifact is cached. The table covers ordinary Tensor and scalar arguments; exact specialization rules depend on the Triton version and backend.
+
+| Input or configuration | Specialization trigger |
+| --- | --- |
+| `tl.constexpr` | Compile-time value changes. |
+| Tensor dtype | Pointer element type changes. |
+| Tensor address | Alignment class changes; the full address is not the key. |
+| Tensor shape / stride | Changes affect separately passed scalars, constexpr values, alignment or compiler options. |
+| Runtime integer | Inferred type or default specialization class changes, such as exact `1`, multiples of `16`, or other values. |
+| Runtime float / bool | Type changes; values alone do not specialize unless passed as constexpr. |
+| Optional argument | Switching between `None` and a Tensor changes the signature. |
+| Compiler options | Effective compilation settings change. |
+
+Changing only Tensor contents or the launch grid does not create a new specialization. Source, compiler, target and cache-state changes can also affect artifact reuse.
+
+Specialization controls:
+
+- `do_not_specialize`: suppress value/alignment specialization for selected runtime arguments; type differences and explicit constexpr values still matter.
+- `do_not_specialize_on_alignment`: suppress alignment/divisibility specialization; other specialization remains.
+- Validate accuracy and performance after reducing specialization, then use warmup for required variants.
+
+An `autotune` key selects tuning cases. Retuning and loading a persistent cache are distinct from recompiling a kernel.
+
+References: [Triton JIT API](https://triton-lang.org/main/python-api/generated/triton.jit.html), [autotune API](https://triton-lang.org/main/python-api/generated/triton.autotune.html), [triton-ascend JIT implementation](https://github.com/Ascend/triton-ascend/blob/main/python/triton/runtime/jit.py), [backend specialization](https://github.com/Ascend/triton-ascend/blob/main/python/triton/backends/compiler.py), [compilation cache](https://github.com/Ascend/triton-ascend/blob/main/python/triton/compiler/compiler.py).

[Doc][Misc] Update AGENTS.md development guidelines (#22106)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR updates the `AGENTS.md` development guidelines to align with the
latest project practices, specifically:
- Replaces environment variables with the recommended additional
configuration mechanism (`--additional-config`).
- Clarifies configuration review requirements for both additional config
keys and environment variables.
- Outlines testing procedures that can be performed without NPU
hardware.
- References specific agent skills (`vllm-ascend-model-adapter` and
`vllm-ascend-release`).
- Clarifies PR title formatting and template expectations.

No, this is a documentation-only update.

FULL_DECODE_ONLY. Preserve the existing model, performance/accuracy
datasets, concurrency, sampling and dispatch name. StaticKernel weekly
is unchanged.

successful final ReplaySSM configuration, threshold0.95

concurrency128; AIME2025 remains concurrency32, baseline95/absolute
tolerance10. Keep the existing model alias and framework-managed
interfaces, ports and proxy adaptations.

implementation rejects int8 for this indexer. This PR does not add the
RC1 indexer implementation or change inference code.

release-note fragment.

[BugFix][Kernel] Fix A5 SWA indices during bounded replay (#21952)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

After a prefix-cache hit, bounded replay limits each causal SWA row to
KV positions at or after its replay floor. The A5 path built explicit
indices for the full window and then reduced only the visible length.
QSMLA consumes the first N indices, so it selected older positions that
could fall before the replay floor.

Build the A5 indices and their lengths from the same replay-clipped
window.
Keep the valid indices at the start of each row and leave inactive
entries
as -1. The scalar-band and noncausal paths retain their existing
semantics.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. A5 now reads the intended SWA KV positions during bounded replay.
The CLI and existing configuration remain compatible.

### How was this patch tested?

- CPU regression: **5 passed**; the two replay cases fail on unpatched
`main`.
Command: `pytest -q --confcutdir=tests/ut/attention
tests/ut/attention/test_a5_swa_replay_cpu.py`.
- Patch application, diff, Python syntax and changed-file pre-commit
checks passed.
Full `bash format.sh ci` reports existing ShellCheck `SC2218` errors in
unchanged scripts.
- Provided A5 results on **v0.32.0rc1** (not rerun on `main`): the index
regression
reproduced 128 incorrect rows out of 131 before the fix and passed after
it.
  GSM8K 200-shot, concurrency 512, three runs per arm:
baseline **97.27%, 95.30%, 95.45%**; patched **97.27%, 96.89%, 97.27%**.
- Added numerical A5 kernel regression tests; not run locally because no
A5 is available.
The existing replay UT could not collect because `vllm` is not installed
locally.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: Added replay-floor, padding,
  empty/single-token, window-size and visible-length boundary coverage.
- [x] **Regression test**: Added CPU composition cases that fail on the
  unmodified main branch, and a numerical A5 kernel regression for CI.
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: No new exception or timeout
behavior;
  numerical length limits are covered by the added NPU tests.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: Tests check the KV prefix
consumed by
QSMLA and verify that ordinary causal and noncausal behavior is
preserved.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: Main-branch hardware performance
validation has
not been run locally. The provided rc1 A/B evidence is accuracy
validation.

+def _assert_rows(indices, lengths, expected, window_size):
+    rows = indices.squeeze(1).cpu().tolist()
+    counts = lengths.flatten().cpu().tolist()
+    assert indices.dtype == lengths.dtype == torch.int32
+    assert counts == [len(row) for row in expected]
+    assert rows == [row + [-1] * (window_size - len(row)) for row in expected]

+        torch.tensor([33920, 2, 640], dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE),
+        torch.tensor([33792, 0, 639], dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE),
+        len(query_positions),
+    )
+    normal_indices, normal_lengths = build_window_indices_triton(positions, WINDOW)
+    expected_normal = [list(range(max(0, p - WINDOW + 1), p + 1)) for p in query_positions + [0, 0]]
+    _assert_rows(normal_indices, normal_lengths, expected_normal, WINDOW)
+
+    expected_replay = [list(range(33792, p + 1)) for p in range(33792, 33920)]
+    expected_replay += [[0], [0, 1], [639], [], []]
+    indices_output = torch.full_like(normal_indices, 12345)

+# build_window_indices_triton
+
+## Description
+
+- Function. Build a fixed-width row of logical KV positions and a valid count
+  for each query in causal sliding-window attention (SWA). The A5 mixed-quant
+  sparse attention operator consumes the first `length` entries of each row.
+- Formula. For query position `p` and window size `W`, the ordinary count is
+  `base = min(p + 1, W)`. When a visible count `v` is supplied, the count is
+  `length = min(base, max(v, 0))`. Otherwise, `length = base`.
+  The first valid position is `start = p + 1 - length`.
+- Algorithm flow. One Triton program handles one query row. It computes the
+  count, writes `start + column` in the first `length` columns, fills the
+  remaining columns with `-1`, and writes the same count to the length tensor.
+- Supported modes. Ascend A5, on the DeepSeek-V4.1 packed-cache attention path.
+
+During bounded replay, the metadata builder computes a visible count per real
+query using the request's replay boundary `r`. The first readable position is
+`max(0, p - W + 1, r)`, and the count is `p - first_readable_position + 1`
+for a query in the replayed range. Applying that count before generating the
+row makes the first entry agree with the replay boundary.
+
+## Parameters
+
+`T` is the number of input rows, including any padding, and `W` is the
+window width. The function returns `(indices, lengths)`.
+
+| Parameter | Input/Output/Attribute | Description | Data type | Data format |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| `positions` | Input | Logical query positions `[T]`, flattened in batch order. | INT64 | ND |
+| `window_size` | Attribute | Positive window width `W`, including the current token. | Python int | Scalar |
+| `visible_lengths` | Optional input | One visible KV count per real query row, in the same order as `positions`. Defaults to `None`. | INT32 | ND, `[T_real]` or `[T_real, 1]` |
+| `indices_output` | Optional output | Caller-provided buffer for the returned indices. A buffer is allocated when omitted. | INT32 | ND, `[T, 1, W]` |
+| `lengths_output` | Optional output | Caller-provided buffer for the returned valid counts. A buffer is allocated when omitted. | INT32 | ND, `[T, 1]` |
+
+## Constraints
+
+- Supply non-negative logical token positions representable as INT32 and a
+  positive `window_size`. Empty input returns empty outputs without a kernel
+  launch.
+- When `visible_lengths` is supplied, the counts describe the leading real
+  query rows. Rows beyond `visible_lengths.numel()` have length zero and all
+  indices set to `-1`. A negative count also produces an empty row, and a count
+  above the ordinary window length is clipped to that length.
+- Supply all tensors on the same NPU. Caller-provided output buffers must be
+  contiguous with the shapes and dtypes above. The function writes into and
+  returns those buffers, allowing graph replay callers to retain their
+  addresses.
+
+## Origin and Differences
+
+- Origin. vLLM Ascend's existing causal window index builder for the A5
+  packed-cache path.
+- Differences. The replay path clips the ordinary count before generating the
+  indices. This preserves the newest readable KV positions at the start of
+  each row. When the optional counts are omitted, the kernel uses the ordinary
+  causal window.
+
+## Test Cases
+
+The A5 single-card test checks exact INT32 indices and counts at the model's
+128-token window size, including mixed requests, the replay boundary, padded
+rows, and reuse of output buffers. It also checks empty input, non-contiguous
+visible counts, negative and oversized counts, and a non-power-of-two window.
+
+```bash
+pytest -sv tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_build_window_indices.py
+```
+
+## Example
+
+With `positions = [11, 0]`, `window_size = 4`, and `visible_lengths = [2]`,
+the first row is `[10, 11, -1, -1]` with count 2. The second row is padding
+and contains four `-1` entries with count 0. The ordinary window for position
+11 would contain `[8, 9, 10, 11]`.

[Ops][Feature] Support SWIGLUSTEP activation in W8A8 MXFP8 dynamic fused MoE (#21550)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

The W8A8 MXFP8 dynamic fused MoE path previously ran SWIGLUSTEP
activation and MXFP8 quantization separately. This PR fuses them with
`npu_swiglu_mx_quant` using `swiglu_mode=3`, which matches SWIGLUSTEP's
post-SiLU clamp behavior.

The fused operator receives per-expert token counts through
`group_index`. The clamp limit defaults to `7.0` when the input value is
missing, `None`, or zero. The existing SwiGLU-OAI behavior is preserved.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No, this is an internal quantization dispatch optimization for Ascend
NPU.

### How was this patch tested?

**Accuracy Evaluation**

GPQA accuracy evaluation was performed on Step 3.7 and Minimax M3.1
Flash to verify that the fused SWIGLUSTEP activation and MXFP8
quantization path introduces no accuracy regression.

| Model | Baseline | With this PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Step 3.7 | 80.81% | 80.81% |
| Minimax M3.1 Flash | 87.88% | 87.88% |

No accuracy regression was observed on either model.

**Performance Evaluation**

Performance benchmarking was conducted to compare the original separate
SWIGLUSTEP activation and Dynamic MXFP8 quantization operators against
the fused `npu_swiglu_mx_quant` operator.

| Implementation | Average Latency |
| --- | ---: |
| Baseline: `_swiglustep_kernel` + `DynamicMxQuant` | 10.765 μs |
| With this PR: `npu_swiglu_mx_quant` | 6.030 μs |

The fused operator reduces average latency from 10.765 μs to 6.030 μs,
achieving a 43.98% latency reduction compared to the original separate
operators. These results demonstrate that fusing SWIGLUSTEP activation
and MXFP8 quantization provides a measurable performance benefit.

**Unit Tests**

Added unit coverage for activation dispatch, both scale algorithms,
count and cumulative group lists, operator arguments, and GMM2 scale
propagation in
`tests/ut/quantization/methods/w8a8/test_swiglu_mx_quant.py`.

[BugFix][Spec Decode] Preserve DeepSeek V4 DSpark heads during weight loading (#17095)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fixes #17094.

DeepSeek V4 DSpark maps both target and MTP-specific head/embed/HC
checkpoint keys to the same parameters. If `mtp.2.head.weight` arrives
before the target `head.weight`, the latter silently overwrites the
trained draft head. Unordered shard completion can therefore collapse
acceptance while requests still succeed.

This change gives MTP-specific parameters priority independently of
loading order:

- Track the five head/embed/HC destination names already loaded from
`mtp.*`.
- Skip subsequent target fallbacks for those parameters; allow later MTP
weights to replace earlier fallbacks.
- Preserve standalone and partial-MTP fallback behavior and the existing
rotation guards, without buffering checkpoint tensors.

The September 7 W8A8 checkpoint's `optional: {}` exposes the target
head/embed fallback path. This is a loader correctness fix, not a change
to checkpoint metadata, the forward path, or acceptance rules. The issue
contains a tiny checkpoint-free reproducer, the checkpoint comparison,
and the regression history (#13506).

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes: checkpoints containing dedicated MTP heads consistently use those
heads regardless of shard order, restoring speculative acceptance. There
are no new flags or API changes. Target weights remain fallbacks when
the corresponding MTP weights are absent.

### How was this patch tested?

- Added `tests/ut/model_executor/test_dspark_head_loading.py`: **262
passed**, covering explicit target-first/draft-first order, 128 seeded
shuffles, rotation present/absent, target-only fallback, and partial MTP
heads. The PR's complete model module was imported into the existing
Ascend test environment; only parallel-state accessors are mocked by the
tests.
- Negative control using the unmodified main model module: **243 failed,
19 passed**. The minimal issue reproducer produces `1.0 / 7.0` before
the fix and `7.0 / 7.0` after it.
- `bash format.sh ci`: passed (rerun after the shellcheck bootstrap
encountered a concurrent download/extraction error).
- Hardware validation of this same loader fix on the pinned nightly
stack: two 8 x 910B3 hosts, TP8 / K7, EP off/on; fresh model reloads
verified all 8 TP draft-head shards and all HC parameters against the
checkpoint, without runtime weight repair.
- Real-workload C1/C8: **512 formal requests passed** across two
consecutive warm 64-request batches per configuration/concurrency. C1
request-mean **pure decode TPOT**, excluding TTFT/prefill, recovered
from **48.70 to 12.20 ms (EP off)** and **49.16 to 12.50 ms (EP on)**.
This is recovery from corrupted draft weights, not a speedup over an
already-correct model.

Hardware measurements used Ascend `44f9bf53d` / vLLM `2cf0a6915` with
this loader fix. This PR is based on main `0003e1b75`; its
loader/remapper method ASTs are identical to the hardware-validated fix.
The complete latest-main serving stack has not been re-benchmarked.

[Community]Update agent guide for release note write (#22061)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR updates the developer guidelines (`AGENTS.md`) and the release
notes documentation (`release_notes/README.md`,
`release_notes/TEMPLATE.yaml`) to provide clearer, more actionable
instructions on how to write release note fragments. Specifically, it
emphasizes writing from the user's perspective, avoiding implementation
details, and providing concrete details for performance, breaking
changes, and bug fixes.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No, this is a documentation-only update.

[Misc][KV Transfer] Add concise heartbeat logs for MooncakeConnectorV2 (#21867)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

The renewable leases introduced in #21425 report failures but provide
little visibility into normal heartbeat delivery and lease handling. Add
three concise log events for MooncakeConnectorV2:

- D emits one DEBUG `event=send` after each successful batch send, with
the producer endpoint and request count. No successful ACK logs or
request-ID lists are added.

- P emits one DEBUG `event=process` per heartbeat batch, counting
extended, unchanged, expired, and unknown request IDs. An unchanged
deadline is a valid outcome when the existing lease already lasts long
enough.

- P emits `event=lease_finish` once per completed lease: DEBUG for DONE,
ERROR for expiry with `expired_by_s`. Expiry logs retain the original
`Force freed expired Mooncake request ... after KV lease expired` prefix
for existing log searches, followed by structured fields including
`action=queued_for_release` to clarify the scheduler handoff.

Logging runs outside the lease state locks and uses deferred formatting.
The existing heartbeat failure warning now includes the exception type
and reason. No new configuration, periodic summaries, per-request
history, or wire-protocol changes are introduced.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Diagnostic logging only. Normal events require DEBUG logging; lease
expiry remains ERROR. Lease timing, renewal, ACK handling, and release
decisions are unchanged. No release-note fragment is included because
`release_notes/README.md` explicitly exempts internal logging changes.

### How was this patch tested?

- Added eight focused cases covering mixed/empty heartbeat outcomes,
exactly-once completion through DONE and both expiry paths, logging
outside state locks, and successful 512+1 batching after nonblocking
backpressure without ACK success logs.

- At head `4d7ad7169`, GitHub pre-commit and both CPU unit-test jobs
(pinned vLLM main and v0.33.0) passed. The CI gate still requires a
maintainer-selected test label; selected NPU CI jobs have not run.

- On Ascend A3, `python -m pytest -q
tests/ut/kv_offload/mooncake_v2/test_pull_scheduler.py` passed: **137
passed**.

- Ran a 35-minute GLM-5.3-Flash W8A8 1P1D validation with a 131072-token
context limit, 128 concurrent background requests, 65536-token inputs,
and 32768-token generation budgets. All 128 first-wave requests reported
58880 cached prompt tokens (89.84%). The client resumed decode
recomputation using exact output token IDs; 81 background requests
completed the full 32768 tokens before validation ended, then
outstanding background requests were cancelled deliberately.

- Three 64K-input content probes submitted during the load retained
their P-side KV for **1615.46 / 1616.08 / 1615.68 seconds**, exceeding
the former 480-second threshold, and ended their leases through DONE.
All three returned the expected verification code, integer arithmetic
result, Chinese city name, and request identifier. The idle baseline
also passed.

- Observed 105 D send logs, 105 P processing logs, and 222 lease-finish
logs (including cleanup), totaling 83342 bytes. Heartbeats extended
leases 8204 times; normal-load expired/unknown counts were zero, with no
ACK success logs or server logging errors. A separate P-only request
with no D heartbeat expired after approximately 120 seconds and emitted
the preserved force-free ERROR prefix.

Runtime validation used an existing r93 openEuler container with this
exact PR source and the pinned vLLM source tree. Only heartbeat DEBUG
records plus ordinary INFO-and-higher records were enabled: unfiltered
shared-logger DEBUG exposed an unrelated existing MoE `%d`/`None`
formatting error. This validates heartbeat observability under load, not
globally enabling all DEBUG logs. No old-version inference A/B
comparison or controlled logging-overhead benchmark is claimed.

### Checklist

- [x] Boundary and error-path coverage added.

- [x] Targeted remote unit tests, Linux pre-commit, and both CPU CI jobs
pass.

- [x] Real NPU pressure validation confirms renewal beyond 480 seconds,
content correctness, and the three log events.

- [ ] Maintainer-selected NPU CI gate completed (requires a
test-selection label).

- [ ] Performance impact measured (no controlled logging-on/off
comparison).

[CI][Build] Bump CANN base images to 9.3.0_20261113161300 (#22008)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Reproduce the Dockerfile changes from #21879 on current main. Update all
eight root Dockerfiles (A2/A3/310P/A5, Ubuntu/openEuler) from
`quay.io/ascend/cann:9.2.1-*` to
`swr.cn-north-12.myhuaweicloud.com/atlas_inference/cann:9.3.0_20261113161300-*`,
preserving the SoC, OS and Python 3.12 suffixes.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Docker images will use CANN 9.3.0_20261113161300 instead of 9.2.1.

### How was this patch tested?

- `git apply --check` passed for the original #21879 patch on current
main.
- Verified all eight Dockerfiles contain exactly the intended FROM
replacement and no other changes.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- `bash format.sh ci` could not run because `pre-commit` is not
installed.
- Image builds and NPU runtime validation have not been run locally and
remain for CI/review before merge. No runtime tests were added for this
base-image-only update.

### Checklist

- [x] Reviewed test applicability; boundary, regression, error-path and
performance tests do not apply to this Dockerfile version update.
- [x] CI image builds and NPU validation completed.

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/ba15685ab7f4f5fbed8630bbb7441f8837e76fbe

Signed-off-by: t00911734 <tangdafu@huawei.com>
Co-authored-by: t00911734 <tangdafu@huawei.com>
